title.zh: 卷一百十四 列傳第六十四: 魯炅 裴茙 來瑱 周智光
title.en: Volume 114 Biographies 64: Lu Jiong, Pei Rong, Lai Zhen, Zhou Zhiguan
title.raw: 卷一百十四 列傳第六十四: 魯炅 裴茙 來瑱 周智光 Volume 114 Biographies 64: Lu Jiong, Pei Rong, Lai Zhen, Zhou Zhiguan

sentences.zh: 元載元載，鳳翔岐山人也，家本寒微。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai was a native of Qishan in Fengxiang; his family was originally humble and poor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai came from Qishan in Fengxiang; his family had always been of modest means.

sentences.zh: 父景昇，任員外官，不理產業，常居岐州。

translations.literal: His father Jing Sheng held a supernumerary office, did not manage the family property, and usually lived in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing Sheng held an extra-quota court post, paid no attention to the family estate, and lived for the most part in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 載母攜載適景昇，冒姓元氏。

translations.literal: Zai's mother brought Zai when she married Jing Sheng, and they took the surname Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai's mother married Jing Sheng, she brought the boy with her, and the family adopted the surname Yuan.

sentences.zh: 載自幼嗜學，好屬文，性敏惠，博覽子史，尤學道書。

translations.literal: From childhood Zai loved study, delighted in literary composition, was by nature quick and clever, read widely in the histories, and especially studied Daoist texts.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was devoted to learning, fond of writing, and gifted by nature; he read widely in history and devoted particular attention to Daoist writings.

sentences.zh: 家貧，徒步隨鄉賦，累上不升第。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he went on foot to take the provincial examinations and repeatedly failed to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Because the family was poor, he walked to the capital to sit for the examinations, but try after try he failed to win a degree.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，玄宗崇奉道教，下詔求明莊、老、文、列四子之學者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, Xuanzong revered Daoism and issued an edict seeking scholars versed in the Zhuangzi, Laozi, Wenzi, and Liezi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign, Emperor Xuanzong, who had embraced Daoism, issued an edict calling for scholars expert in the Zhuangzi, Laozi, Wenzi, and Liezi.

sentences.zh: 載策入高科，授邠州新平尉。

translations.literal: Zai's examination essay placed in the highest grade, and he was appointed Defender of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zai's examination essay won the highest grade, and he was appointed defender of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 監察御史韋鎰充使監選黔中，引載為判官，載名稍著，遷大理評事。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Wei Yi served as commissioner overseeing selection in Qianzhong and took Zai as his aide; Zai's name gradually became known, and he was promoted to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Investigating Censor Wei Yi went to Qianzhong as commissioner overseeing the selection examinations, he took Zai on as his aide. Zai's reputation slowly spread, and he was promoted to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 東都留守苗晉卿又引為判官，遷大理司直。

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing, Eastern Capital Protector, also took him as an aide, and he was promoted to rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing, protector of the Eastern Capital, likewise took him on as an aide, after which he was promoted to rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，急於軍務，諸道廉使隨才擢用。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, he was urgent about military affairs and promoted regional inspectors according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong came to the throne, military affairs took precedence, and regional inspectors were promoted wherever talent was found.

sentences.zh: 時載避地江左，蘇州刺史、江東采訪使李希言表載為副，拜祠部員外郎，遷洪州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Zai had fled to the lower Yangzi; Li Xiyan, prefect of Suzhou and Jiangdong investigating commissioner, recommended Zai as his deputy. He was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Rites and later transferred to prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had taken refuge south of the Yangzi. Li Xiyan, prefect of Suzhou and Jiangdong investigating commissioner, recommended him as deputy; he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Rites and later became prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，入為度支郎中。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he entered the capital as director in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, he was summoned to the capital as director in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 載智性敏悟，善奏對，肅宗嘉之，委以國計，俾充使江、淮，都領漕輓之任，尋加御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zai was quick and perceptive by nature and skilled at audience responses; Suzong was pleased with him, entrusted him with state finance, made him commissioner to the Jiang and Huai regions to oversee transport of grain tribute, and soon added him as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and adept at answering in audience, Zai won Suzong's favor. The emperor entrusted him with the national accounts, sent him as commissioner to the Jiang and Huai regions to oversee grain transport, and soon named him vice censor-in-chief as well.

sentences.zh: 數月徵入，遷戶部侍郎、度支使並諸道轉運使。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was recalled and promoted to vice minister of revenue, commissioner of revenue, and commissioner of transport for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was recalled and promoted to vice minister of revenue, with concurrent appointment as commissioner of revenue and transport commissioner for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 既至朝廷，會肅宗寢疾。

translations.literal: Once he reached court, Suzong fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he arrived at court, Emperor Suzong fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 載與幸臣李輔國善。

translations.literal: Zai was on good terms with the favored minister Li Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was on close terms with the emperor's favorite, Li Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 輔國妻元氏，載之諸宗，因是相昵狎。

translations.literal: Fuguo's wife was of the Yuan clan, a kinswoman of Zai's, and because of this they were intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo's wife belonged to the Yuan clan and was related to Zai, which drew the two men into close intimacy.

sentences.zh: 時輔國權傾海內，舉無違者，會選京尹，輔國乃以載兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: At that time Fuguo's power dominated the realm and none dared oppose him. When the capital intendant was to be chosen, Fuguo had Zai appointed concurrently as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo's power then dominated the empire, and none dared defy him. When a new capital intendant was to be chosen, he had Zai appointed concurrently as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 載意屬國柄，詣輔國懇辭京尹，輔國識其意，然之。

translations.literal: Zai's aim was the chief ministership; he went to Fuguo and earnestly declined the post of capital intendant. Fuguo understood his intent and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had his eye on the chief ministership. He went to Li Fuguo and earnestly declined the capital intendant post; Fuguo understood what he wanted and agreed.

sentences.zh: 翌日拜載同中書門下平章事，度支轉運使如故。

translations.literal: The next day Zai was appointed associate chief minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, while his posts as revenue and transport commissioner remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zai was appointed associate chief minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, while retaining his posts as revenue and transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旬日，肅宗晏駕，代宗即位，輔國勢愈重，稱載於上前。

translations.literal: Within ten days Suzong died; Daizong succeeded to the throne. Fuguo's power grew still greater, and he praised Zai before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Emperor Suzong died and Daizong succeeded him. Li Fuguo's power grew still greater, and he spoke highly of Zai before the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 載能伺上意，頗承恩遇，遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，加集賢殿大學士，修國史。

translations.literal: Zai could discern the emperor's wishes and received considerable favor; he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, associate chief minister, made grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at reading the emperor's mind, Zai enjoyed considerable favor. He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and associate chief minister, made grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 又加銀青光祿大夫，封許昌縣子。

translations.literal: He was further given the silver-blue-girdled Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Viscount of Xuchang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to silver-blue-girdled Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Viscount of Xuchang County.

sentences.zh: 載以度支轉運使職務繁碎，負荷且重，慮傷名，阻大位，素與劉晏相友善，乃悉以錢穀之務委之，薦晏自代，載自加營田使。

translations.literal: Zai considered the duties of revenue and transport commissioner numerous and trivial yet burdensome, feared they would harm his reputation and block his rise to the highest office, had long been friendly with Liu Yan, and therefore entrusted all fiscal affairs to him, recommending Yan to replace himself, while Zai took the additional post of commissioner of garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: Zai felt that the revenue and transport posts were tedious yet heavy burdens that might tarnish his reputation and block his path to supreme power. He had long been friendly with Liu Yan, so he handed all fiscal duties over to him and recommended Yan as his replacement, while taking the additional post of commissioner of garrison fields for himself.

sentences.zh: 李輔國罷職，又加判天下元帥行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Li Fuguo was removed from office, Zai was additionally made acting chief of staff to the commander-in-chief of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Fuguo was dismissed, Zai was additionally appointed acting chief of staff to the commander-in-chief of all armies.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，與宰臣劉晏、裴遵慶同扈從至陜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, he accompanied the chief ministers Liu Yan and Pei Zunqing in escorting the emperor to Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangde (763), he accompanied the chief ministers Liu Yan and Pei Zunqing when the emperor withdrew to Shaan.

sentences.zh: 及輿駕還宮，遵慶皆罷所任，載恩寵彌盛。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, Zunqing and the others were all dismissed from their posts, while Zai's favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Pei Zunqing and the others were all dismissed, while Zai's favor only grew.

sentences.zh: 輔國死，載復結內侍董秀，多與之金帛，委主書卓英倩潛通密旨。

translations.literal: After Fuguo died, Zai again cultivated the palace attendant Dong Xiu, gave him much gold and silk, and entrusted the chief clerk Zhuo Yingqian to convey secret edicts in private.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Fuguo's death, Zai cultivated the eunuch Dong Xiu, lavished gold and silk on him, and used chief clerk Zhuo Yingqian to pass secret messages to and from the throne.

sentences.zh: 以是上有所屬，載必先知之，承意探微，言必玄合，上益信任之。

translations.literal: Thus whenever the emperor had a preference, Zai always knew it beforehand; he followed the intent and probed subtleties, and his words always matched mysteriously well, so the emperor trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor formed a preference, Zai already knew it. He anticipated intent and probed every subtlety; his words always struck the mark, and the emperor trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 妻王氏狠戾自專，載出朝謁，縱子伯和等遊於外，上封人顧繇奏之，上方任載以政，反罪繇而已。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Wang was fierce and willful; when Zai went out to court audience, she let their sons Bohe and others roam outside. The sealed memorialist Gu Yao reported this, but the emperor was then relying on Zai for government and punished only Yao.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Wang was fierce and domineering. While Zai attended court, she let their sons Bohe and the others roam the city at will. Memorialist Gu Yao reported this, but the emperor was then relying on Zai for government and punished Yao instead.

sentences.zh: 內侍魚朝恩負恃權寵，不與載協，載常憚之。

translations.literal: The palace attendant Yu Chaoen relied on favor and power, did not cooperate with Zai, and Zai often feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yu Chaoen relied on imperial favor and power, would not work with Zai, and Zai often feared him.

sentences.zh: 大曆四年冬，乘間密奏朝恩專權不軌，請除之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Dali, seizing an opportunity he secretly memorialized that Chaoen monopolized power and acted unlawfully, and asked that he be removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year of Dali (769), he seized an opportunity to memorialize secretly that Yu Chaoen monopolized power and acted unlawfully, and asked that he be removed.

sentences.zh: 朝恩驕橫，天下咸怒，上亦知之，及聞載奏，適會於心。

translations.literal: Chaoen was arrogant and overbearing; all under Heaven were angry, and the emperor knew it as well. When he heard Zai's memorial, it exactly matched his own mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chaoen was arrogant and overbearing; the empire seethed with anger, and the emperor knew it. When he read Zai's memorial, it matched exactly what he had been thinking.

sentences.zh: 載遂結北軍大將同謀，以防萬慮。

translations.literal: Zai then joined in conspiracy with generals of the northern armies to guard against every contingency.
translations.idiomatic: Zai then conspired with generals of the northern armies to guard against every contingency.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，朝恩伏法，度支使第五琦以朝恩黨坐累，載兼判度支，志氣自若，謂己有除惡之功，是非前賢，以為文武才略，莫己之若。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year Chaoen was executed according to law. The revenue commissioner Diwu Qi was implicated as Chaoen's partisan; Zai took concurrent charge of revenue. His spirit was as before; he considered himself to have the merit of removing evil, disparaged former worthies, and believed that in civil and military talent none could equal him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year (770), Yu Chaoen was executed. Revenue Commissioner Diwu Qi was implicated as his partisan, and Zai took over revenue affairs as well. He was as self-assured as ever, convinced that he had rid the court of a great evil, dismissive of earlier worthies, and certain that no one matched his civil and military gifts.

sentences.zh: 外委胥吏，內聽婦言。

translations.literal: Outwardly he entrusted affairs to clerks; inwardly he heeded his wife's words.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he left affairs to clerks; inwardly he obeyed his wife.

sentences.zh: 城中開南北二甲第，室宇宏麗，冠絕當時。

translations.literal: Within the city he opened two great mansions, north and south; their halls were grand and splendid, unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he built two great mansions, north and south, whose halls were grand and splendid beyond anything of the age.

sentences.zh: 又於近郊起亭榭，所至之處，帷帳什器，皆於宿設，儲不改供。

translations.literal: He also raised pavilions in the near suburbs; wherever he went, curtains, furnishings, and utensils were all set out the night before, and stores were kept stocked without change.
translations.idiomatic: He also built pavilions in the suburbs. Wherever he went, curtains, furnishings, and utensils were set out the night before, and stores were kept fully stocked.

sentences.zh: 城南膏腴別墅，連疆接畛，凡數十所，婢仆曳羅綺一百餘人，恣為不法，侈僭無度。

translations.literal: South of the city were rich suburban villas, their boundaries joining for dozens of estates; more than a hundred maidservants and attendants trailed in silks. They did as they pleased outside the law, extravagant and presumptuous beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city he owned dozens of rich suburban estates whose boundaries ran together. More than a hundred maidservants and attendants dressed in silks; they broke the law at will in extravagance and presumption beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 江、淮方面，京輦要司，皆排去忠良，引用貪猥。

translations.literal: In the Jiang and Huai regions and in key offices of the capital, he drove out the loyal and good and installed the greedy and base.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiang and Huai regions and in key offices of the capital, he drove out the loyal and installed the greedy and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 士有求進者，不結子弟，則謁主書，貨賄公行，近年以來，未有其比。

translations.literal: Scholars seeking advancement, if they did not attach themselves to his sons, would visit his chief clerks; bribes were openly exchanged. In recent years there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars seeking office had to cultivate his sons or bribe his chief clerks; graft was open and rampant. In recent years there had been nothing like it.

sentences.zh: 與王縉同列，縉方務聚財，遂睦於載，二人相得甚歡，日益縱橫。

translations.literal: He served alongside Wang Jin; Jin was then bent on amassing wealth and therefore became close with Zai. The two were very pleased with each other and grew ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He served alongside Wang Jin, who was then bent on amassing wealth; the two became close allies and grew ever more unrestrained together.

sentences.zh: 代宗盡察其跡，以載任寄多年，欲全君臣之分，載嘗獨見，上誡之，不悛。

translations.literal: Daizong fully perceived his conduct, but because Zai had been entrusted for many years wished to preserve the bond between ruler and minister. Zai was once received in private audience and admonished by the emperor, yet he did not repent.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong saw through all of this, but because Zai had served him for many years he wished to preserve the bond between ruler and minister. Once he received Zai in private audience and admonished him, yet Zai did not repent.

sentences.zh: 初，扈駕自陜還，與縉上表，請以河中府為中都，秋杪行幸，春首還京，以避蕃戎侵軼之患。

translations.literal: Earlier, when escorting the emperor back from Shaan, he and Jin submitted a memorial asking that Hezhong Prefecture be made the central capital, with the emperor traveling there in late autumn and returning to the capital in early spring, to avoid the calamity of Tibetan and Rong incursions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when escorting the emperor back from Shaan, he and Jin had memorialized that Hezhong Prefecture be made a secondary capital, with the court moving there in late autumn and returning in early spring to escape Tibetan raids.

sentences.zh: 帝初納之，遣條奏以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor at first accepted it and ordered a detailed memorial submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first accepted the proposal and ordered a detailed plan submitted.

sentences.zh: 自魚朝恩就誅，誌頗盈滿，遂抗表請建中都，文多不載。

translations.literal: After Yu Chaoen was executed, his ambition was quite full; he then submitted a defiant memorial requesting establishment of a central capital. Most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Chaoen's execution his ambition swelled, and he submitted a bold memorial calling for a permanent secondary capital. Most of the text is not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 大略以關輔、河東等十州戶稅入奉京師，創置精兵五萬，管在中都，以威四方，辭多開合。

translations.literal: In outline it proposed that household taxes from ten prefectures including Guanfu and Hedong be sent to the capital, that fifty thousand elite troops be newly established and stationed at the central capital to awe the four quarters; the language was largely evasive.
translations.idiomatic: In outline it proposed diverting household taxes from ten prefectures including Guanfu and Hedong to the capital, raising fifty thousand elite troops stationed at the secondary capital to overawe the realm. The language was largely evasive.

sentences.zh: 自以為表入事行，潛遣所由吏於河中經營。

translations.literal: He himself believed that once the memorial entered court the matter would proceed, and secretly sent responsible clerks to Hezhong to make arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Confident that once the memorial was filed the plan would go ahead, he secretly sent clerks to Hezhong to make preparations.

sentences.zh: 節度寄理於涇州。

translations.literal: The military commission was provisionally administered from Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The military commission was provisionally administered from Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年，蕃戎入邠寧之後，朝議以為三輔已西，無襟帶之固，而涇州散地，不足為守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, after the Tibetans and Rong entered Bin and Ning, court opinion held that west of the three metropolitan areas there was no secure strategic belt, while Jing Prefecture was scattered territory insufficient for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali (773), after Tibetan forces entered Bin and Ning, court opinion held that west of the capital region there was no secure defensive belt, and that Jing Prefecture's scattered territory was inadequate for defense.

sentences.zh: 載嘗為西州刺史，知河西、隴右之要害，指畫於上前曰：「今國家西境極於潘源，吐蕃防戍在摧沙堡，而原州界其間。

translations.literal: Zai had once been prefect of Xi Prefecture and knew the strategic points of Hexi and Longyou. He outlined a plan before the emperor, saying: "Now the state's western border extends to Panyuan; Tibetan garrisons are at Cuisha Fort, and Yuan Prefecture lies between them.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had once been prefect of Xi Prefecture and knew the strategic points of Hexi and Longyou. Before the emperor he outlined a plan: "The empire's western border now runs to Panyuan. Tibetan garrisons hold Cuisha Fort, and Yuan Prefecture lies between them.

sentences.zh: 原州當西塞之口，接隴山之固，草肥水甘，舊壘存焉。

translations.literal: Yuan Prefecture stands at the mouth of the western frontier, adjoins the strong position of Long Mountain, has rich grass and sweet water, and old ramparts still remain there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Prefecture stands at the gateway of the western frontier, adjoins the strong position of Long Mountain, has rich grass and sweet water, and old ramparts still stand there.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃比毀其垣墉，棄之不居。

translations.literal: The Tibetans have recently destroyed its walls and abandoned it without occupying it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans have recently destroyed its walls and abandoned it without occupying it.

sentences.zh: 其西則監牧故地，皆有長濠巨塹，重復深固。

translations.literal: To its west are the old pasture lands of the imperial stud; all have long moats and great ditches, layered and deeply fortified.
translations.idiomatic: To its west lie the old imperial pasture lands, all with long moats and great ditches, layered defenses dug deep.

sentences.zh: 原州雖早霜，黍稷不藝，而有平涼附其東，獨耕一縣，可以足食。

translations.literal: Though Yuan Prefecture has early frost and millet and panicled millet are not cultivated, Pingliang adjoins it on the east; farming that one county alone can supply enough food.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yuan Prefecture has early frost and grain cannot be grown there, Pingliang adjoins it on the east; farming that one county alone can feed the garrison.

sentences.zh: 請移京西軍戍原州，乘間築之，貯粟一年。

translations.literal: I ask that the metropolitan western army be moved to garrison Yuan Prefecture, that we seize an opportunity to build it up, and store grain for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Move the metropolitan western army to garrison Yuan Prefecture, seize the opportunity to rebuild it, and store a year's grain there.

sentences.zh: 戎人夏牧多在青海，羽書覆至，已逾月矣。

translations.literal: The Rong people's summer pastures are mostly at Qinghai; urgent dispatches have arrived in succession for more than a month already.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians' summer pastures lie mostly at Qinghai; urgent dispatches have been arriving for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 今運築並作，不二旬可畢。

translations.literal: If transport and construction are done together, it can be completed in less than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: If transport and construction proceed together, the work can be finished in less than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 移子儀大軍居涇，以為根本。

translations.literal: Move Guo Ziyi's great army to Jing as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Move Guo Ziyi's main army to Jing as the foundation force.

sentences.zh: 分兵守石門、木峽、隴山之關，北抵於河，皆連山峻嶺，寇不可越。

translations.literal: Divide troops to hold the passes of Shimen, Muxia, and Long Mountain; north to the river—all linked ranges and steep peaks that invaders cannot cross.
translations.idiomatic: Divide troops to hold the passes of Shimen, Muxia, and Long Mountain; north to the Yellow River—all linked ranges and steep peaks that invaders cannot cross.

sentences.zh: 稍置鳴沙縣、豐安軍為之羽翼，北帶靈武五城為之形勢。

translations.literal: Establish Mingxia County and Feng'an Army as supporting wings; to the north link the five cities of Lingwu as strategic posture.
translations.idiomatic: Establish Mingxia County and Feng'an Army as supporting wings; to the north link the five cities of Lingwu into a strategic line.

sentences.zh: 然後舉隴右之地以至安西，是謂斷西戎之脛，朝廷可高枕矣。」

translations.literal: Then raise the lands of Longyou as far as Anxi—this is what is called cutting the shank of the western Rong, and the court may rest its head on a high pillow."
translations.idiomatic: Then advance through Longyou as far as Anxi—cut the shank of the western barbarians, and the court may rest easy."

sentences.zh: 兼圖其地形以獻。

translations.literal: He also submitted a map of the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a map of the terrain.

sentences.zh: 載密使人逾隴山，入原州，量井泉，計徒庸，車乘畚鍤之器皆具。

translations.literal: Zai secretly sent men over Long Mountain into Yuan Prefecture to measure wells and springs, calculate laborers, and prepare carts, baskets, and spades.
translations.idiomatic: Zai secretly sent men over Long Mountain into Yuan Prefecture to survey wells and springs, calculate labor needs, and prepare carts, baskets, and spades.

sentences.zh: 檢校左僕射田神功沮之曰：「夫興師料敵，老將所難。

translations.literal: Acting Left Vice Director Tian Shenggong opposed it, saying: "Raising armies and estimating the enemy are what even veteran generals find difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Left Vice Director Tian Shenggong objected: "Raising armies and estimating the enemy are hard even for veteran generals.

sentences.zh: 陛下信一書生言，舉國從之，聽誤矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty trusts the words of one scholar and would have the whole state follow—if you heed this, you will be mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would trust one scholar's word and commit the whole empire to it—if you heed this, you will be mistaken.

sentences.zh: 上遲疑不決，會載得罪乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and could not decide; when Zai fell from grace the plan was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated and could not decide; when Zai fell from grace the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 初，六年，載條奏應緣別敕授文武六品以下，敕出後望令吏部、兵部便附甲團奏，不得檢勘，從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the sixth year, Zai submitted detailed regulations that appointments of civil and military officials of the sixth rank and below by special edict should, once the edict was issued, be reported by the Ministries of Personnel and War in attached registers for group memorial without examination or verification; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the sixth year (771), Zai memorialized that civil and military appointments of the sixth rank and below made by special edict should, once issued, be reported by the Ministries of Personnel and War in group memorials without review; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時功狀奏擬，結銜多謬，載欲權歸於己，慮有司駁正。

translations.literal: At that time merit reports and proposed appointments often had errors in the linked signatures; Zai wished power to return to himself and feared that the responsible offices would reject and correct them.
translations.idiomatic: Merit reports and proposed appointments often had errors in their linked signatures. Zai wanted power concentrated in his own hands and feared that the responsible offices would reject and correct them.

sentences.zh: 會有上封人李少良密以載醜跡聞，載知之，奏於上前，少良等數人悉斃於公府。

translations.literal: It happened that the sealed memorialist Li Shaoliang secretly reported Zai's shameful conduct. When Zai learned of it, he memorialized before the emperor, and Shaoliang and several others were all beaten to death in the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: A sealed memorialist named Li Shaoliang secretly reported Zai's misconduct. When Zai learned of it, he memorialized before the emperor, and Shaoliang and several others were beaten to death in the government offices.

sentences.zh: 由是道路以目，不敢議載之短。

translations.literal: From this people on the roads exchanged glances with their eyes and dared not discuss Zai's faults.
translations.idiomatic: After that people exchanged fearful glances in the streets and dared not speak of Zai's faults.

sentences.zh: 門庭之內，非其黨與不接，平素交友，涉於道義者悉疏棄之。

translations.literal: Within his gates he received none who were not his partisans; old friends who touched on righteousness he all cast off.
translations.idiomatic: Within his gates he received only partisans; old friends who spoke of righteousness he cast off entirely.

sentences.zh: 代宗寬仁明恕，審其所由，凡累年，載長惡不悛，眾怒上聞。

translations.literal: Daizong was magnanimous, benevolent, clear-sighted, and forgiving; he examined the causes for several years, yet Zai persisted in evil without repentance until public anger reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was magnanimous and clear-sighted; for years he watched Zai persist in evil without repentance until public anger reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 大曆十二年三月庚辰，仗下後，上御延英殿，命左金吾大將軍吳湊收載、縉於政事堂，各留系本所，並中書主事卓英倩、李待榮及載男仲武、季能並收禁，命吏部尚書劉晏訊鞫。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the third month of the twelfth year of Dali, after the court session ended the emperor took the throne at Yanying Hall, ordered Left Golden Guards General Wu Cou to seize Zai and Jin in the Hall of Administration, detain each at his own office, and also arrest Secretariat clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong and Zai's sons Zhongwu and Jineng. He ordered Minister of Personnel Liu Yan to interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the third month of the twelfth year of Dali (777), after court the emperor took the throne at Yanying Hall and ordered Left Golden Guards General Wu Cou to seize Zai and Jin in the Hall of Administration and detain each at his own office. Secretariat clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong and Zai's sons Zhongwu and Jineng were also arrested, and Minister of Personnel Liu Yan was ordered to interrogate them.

sentences.zh: 晏以載受任樹黨，布於天下，不敢專斷，請他官共事。

translations.literal: Yan considered that Zai, once entrusted with office, had planted factions throughout the realm and dared not decide alone; he asked that other officials join in the case.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan felt that Zai, once in power, had planted factions throughout the realm and dared not decide alone; he asked that other officials join the investigation.

sentences.zh: 敕御史大夫李涵、右散騎常侍蕭昕、兵部侍郎袁傪、禮部侍郎常袞、諫議大夫杜亞同推究其狀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kan, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Official Du Ya jointly to investigate the facts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kan, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Official Du Ya to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 辯罪問端，皆出自禁中，仍遣中使詰以陰事，載、縉皆伏罪。

translations.literal: The framing of charges and questions all came from within the palace; palace envoys were still sent to press secret matters, and Zai and Jin both confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The charges and questions all came from within the palace; palace envoys were sent to press secret matters, and both Zai and Jin confessed.

sentences.zh: 是日，宦官左衛將軍、知內侍省事董秀與載同惡，先載於禁中杖殺之。

translations.literal: That same day the eunuch Left Guard General and director of palace attendants Dong Xiu, who shared Zai's evil, was beaten to death in the palace before Zai.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the eunuch Left Guard General and director of palace attendants Dong Xiu, Zai's accomplice, was beaten to death in the palace before Zai himself.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「任直去邪，懸於帝典；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Employing the upright and removing the wicked hangs upon the imperial canon;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Employing the upright and removing the wicked are enjoined by the imperial canon;

sentences.zh: 獎善懲惡，急於時政。

translations.literal: rewarding good and punishing evil is urgent in current governance.
translations.idiomatic: rewarding good and punishing evil are urgent duties of government.

sentences.zh: 和鼎之寄，匪易其人。

translations.literal: The charge of harmonizing the cauldron is not easily given to any man.
translations.idiomatic: The charge of harmonizing the state is not easily entrusted to any man.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事元載，性頗奸回，跡非正直。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister Yuan Zai is by nature quite treacherous and crooked; his conduct is not upright.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister Yuan Zai is by nature treacherous and crooked; his conduct is not upright.

sentences.zh: 寵待逾分，早踐鈞衡。

translations.literal: Favored beyond measure, he early trod the balance of state.
translations.idiomatic: Favored beyond measure, he rose early to the highest offices of state.

sentences.zh: 亮弼之功，未能經邦成務；

translations.literal: In the merit of assisting and enlightening, he has been unable to govern the state and accomplish its tasks;
translations.idiomatic: As a minister assisting the throne, he has failed to govern the state and accomplish its tasks;

sentences.zh: 挾邪之誌，常以罔上面欺。

translations.literal: harboring wicked intent, he has constantly deceived his superiors and mocked the face of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: harboring wicked intent, he has constantly deceived his superiors and mocked the throne.

sentences.zh: 陰托妖巫，夜行解禱，用圖非望，庶逭典章。

translations.literal: He secretly relied on sorcerers and shamans, went out at night to perform rites of release and prayer, sought unlawful ambitions, and hoped to escape the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly relied on sorcerers, went out at night to perform rites of release and prayer, sought unlawful ambitions, and hoped to escape the law.

sentences.zh: 納受贓私，貿鬻官秩。

translations.literal: He accepted bribes and sold offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted bribes and sold offices and ranks.

sentences.zh: 兇妻忍害，暴子侵牟，曾不提防，恣其淩虐。

translations.literal: His fierce wife was cruel and harmful; his violent sons encroached and extorted; he never guarded against them and let them oppress at will.
translations.idiomatic: His fierce wife was cruel; his violent sons extorted and plundered; he never restrained them and let them oppress at will.

sentences.zh: 行僻辭矯，心狠貌恭，使沈抑之流，無因自達，賞罰差謬，罔不由茲。

translations.literal: His conduct was perverse and his words deceptive; his heart was cruel though his appearance respectful. He left the suppressed with no means to advance themselves; errors in rewards and punishments all stemmed from this.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was perverse and his words deceptive; his heart was cruel though his manner respectful. The suppressed had no way to advance; errors in rewards and punishments all stemmed from him.

sentences.zh: 頃以君臣之間，重於去就，冀其遷善，掩而不言。

translations.literal: Recently, because of the bond between ruler and minister, I valued his staying or leaving and hoped he would turn to good, and therefore concealed this without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, valuing the bond between ruler and minister, I hoped he would reform and therefore kept silent.

sentences.zh: 曾無悔非，彌益兇戾，年序滋遠，釁惡貫盈。

translations.literal: He showed no repentance for wrong; he grew ever more fierce and violent as the years lengthened, until offense and evil overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: He showed no repentance; he grew ever more violent as the years passed, until his offenses overflowed.

sentences.zh: 將肅政於朝班，俾申明於憲綱，宜賜自盡。

translations.literal: I shall rectify governance in the court and make clear the law's net; he should be granted death by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: To rectify governance at court and uphold the law, he is ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 朕涉道猶淺，知人不明，理績未彰，遺闕斯眾，致茲刑辟，憫愧良深。

translations.literal: My treading of the Way is still shallow; my knowing of men is not clear; my governing achievements are not yet manifest; omissions and faults are so many that this punishment has been reached—I am deeply moved to pity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: My grasp of the Way is still shallow; my judgment of men has been poor; my achievements in governing are not yet manifest; omissions and faults are so many that this punishment has been reached—I am deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 僶俯行之，務申沮勸，凡在中外，悉朕懷焉。」

translations.literal: Let all diligently carry this out, striving to declare discouragement and encouragement; within and without the court, all should know my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Let all carry this out diligently, striving to declare what is discouraged and what is encouraged; within and without the court, all should know my intent."

sentences.zh: 又制曰：「門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事王縉，附會奸邪，阿諛讒佞。

translations.literal: Another decree said: "Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Chief Minister Wang Jin attached himself to the wicked, flattered and slandered with malice.
translations.idiomatic: Another decree said: "Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Chief Minister Wang Jin attached himself to the wicked, flattered and slandered with malice.

sentences.zh: 據茲犯狀，罪至難容，矜以耋及，未忍加刑。

translations.literal: According to these offenses, his guilt is hard to tolerate; yet in pity for his advanced age I have not borne to impose punishment.
translations.idiomatic: According to these offenses his guilt is intolerable; yet in pity for his advanced age I have not borne to impose capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 俾申屈法之恩，貸以嶽牧之秩。

translations.literal: I thereby extend the grace of bending the law and spare him with the rank of a prefectural governor.
translations.idiomatic: I extend the grace of bending the law and spare him with the rank of a prefectural governor.

sentences.zh: 可使持節括州諸軍事，守括州刺史，宜即赴任。

translations.literal: He is appointed commissioner with credentials for all military affairs of Kuozhou and defender of Kuozhou Prefecture; he should proceed at once to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed commissioner with credentials for all military affairs of Kuozhou and defender of Kuozhou Prefecture; he should proceed at once to his post.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 朕恭己南面，推誠股肱，敷求哲人，將弼予理。

translations.literal: I respectfully hold myself in check facing south, extend sincerity to my arms and legs, broadly seek wise men, and will have them assist my governance.
translations.idiomatic: I hold myself in respectful restraint upon the throne, extend sincerity to my ministers, broadly seek wise men, and will have them assist my governance.

sentences.zh: 昧於任使，過在朕躬，無曠厥官，各慎厥職。」

translations.literal: Blinded in employment and assignment, the fault lies in my person; let no office stand vacant—each guard your duties."
translations.idiomatic: I have been blind in my choice of men; the fault is mine. Let no office stand vacant, and let each of you guard your duties."

sentences.zh: 初，晏等承旨，縉亦處極法，晏謂涵曰：「重刑再覆，國之常典，況誅大臣，豈得不覆奏！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yan and the others received the imperial order, Jin was also to receive the extreme penalty. Yan said to Han: "For heavy punishments to be reviewed twice is the constant canon of the state; how can execution of great ministers proceed without a second memorial!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yan and the others received the imperial order, Jin was also to receive the death penalty. Yan said to Han: "For heavy punishments to be reviewed twice is the constant canon of the state; how can execution of great ministers proceed without a second memorial!

sentences.zh: 又法有首從，二人同刑，亦宜重取進止。」

translations.literal: Moreover the law distinguishes principal and accomplice; when two men share the same penalty, it is also proper to seek the emperor's decision again."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the law distinguishes principal and accomplice; when two men share the same penalty, it is also proper to seek the emperor's decision again."

sentences.zh: 涵等咸聽命。

translations.literal: Han and the others all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Han and the others all obeyed.

sentences.zh: 及晏等覆奏，上乃減縉罪從輕。

translations.literal: When Yan and the others submitted their review memorial, the emperor then reduced Jin's guilt and punished him more lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan and the others submitted their review memorial, the emperor then reduced Jin's guilt and punished him more lightly.

sentences.zh: 載長子 伯和載長子伯和，先是貶在揚州兵曹參軍，載得罪，命中使馳傳於揚州賜死。

translations.literal: Zai's eldest son Bohe—Zai's eldest son Bohe had earlier been demoted to military aide in Yangzhou. When Zai fell from grace, the emperor ordered a palace envoy by express relay to Yangzhou to grant him death.
translations.idiomatic: Zai's eldest son Bohe had earlier been demoted to military aide in Yangzhou. When Zai fell from grace, the emperor ordered a palace envoy by express relay to Yangzhou to grant him death.

sentences.zh: 次子仲武，祠部員外郎，次子季能，秘書省校書郎，並載妻王氏並賜死。

translations.literal: The second son Zhongwu was vice director in the Ministry of Rites; the third son Jineng was collator in the Secretariat. Together with Zai's wife Lady Wang they were all granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Zhongwu was vice director in the Ministry of Rites; the third son Jineng was collator in the Secretariat. Together with Zai's wife Lady Wang they were all ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 女資敬寺尼真一，收入掖庭。

translations.literal: His daughter Zhenyi, a nun at Zijing Temple, was taken into the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Zhenyi, a nun at Zijing Temple, was taken into the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 王氏，開元中河西節度使忠嗣之女也，素以兇戾聞，恣其子伯和等為虐。

translations.literal: Lady Wang was the daughter of Hexi military commissioner Zhongsi in the Kaiyuan era and had long been known for fierceness and willfulness; she let her sons Bohe and the others act tyrannically.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was the daughter of Hexi military commissioner Zhongsi in the Kaiyuan era and had long been known for fierceness and willfulness; she let her sons Bohe and the others act tyrannically.

sentences.zh: 伯和恃父威勢，唯以聚斂財貨，徵求音樂為事。

translations.literal: Bohe relied on his father's power and prestige and devoted himself solely to amassing wealth and seeking out music.
translations.idiomatic: Bohe relied on his father's power and devoted himself solely to amassing wealth and seeking out musicians and entertainers.

sentences.zh: 載在相位多年，權傾四海，外方珍異，皆集其門，資貨不可勝計，故伯和、仲武等得肆其誌。

translations.literal: Zai had been chief minister for many years; his power dominated the four seas. Rare treasures from abroad all gathered at his gate; goods and wealth were beyond counting, so Bohe, Zhongwu, and the others could indulge their desires.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had been chief minister for many years with power that dominated the empire. Rare treasures from abroad gathered at his gate; wealth beyond counting let Bohe, Zhongwu, and the others indulge every desire.

sentences.zh: 輕浮之士，奔其門者，如恐不及。

translations.literal: Frivolous men who rushed to his gate did so as if fearing they would not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Frivolous men rushed to his gate as if afraid they would arrive too late.

sentences.zh: 名姝、異樂，禁中無者有之。

translations.literal: Famous beauties and exotic music—some that the inner palace did not possess.
translations.idiomatic: They had famous beauties and exotic music that not even the inner palace possessed.

sentences.zh: 兄弟各貯妓妾於室，倡優偎褻之戲，天倫同觀，略無愧恥。

translations.literal: The brothers each kept courtesans and concubines in their rooms; actors performed intimate and indecent plays, and the whole family watched together with hardly a trace of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Each brother kept courtesans in his rooms; actors performed indecent plays that the whole family watched together without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 及得罪，行路無嗟惜者。

translations.literal: When they fell from grace, travelers on the road showed no sigh of regret.
translations.idiomatic: When they fell from grace, no one on the roads sighed in regret.

sentences.zh: 中使董秀、主書卓英倩、李待榮及陰陽人李季連，以載之故，皆處極法。

translations.literal: The palace envoy Dong Xiu, chief clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong, and the yin-yang master Li Jilian, because of Zai's case, all received the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy Dong Xiu, chief clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong, and the yin-yang master Li Jilian were all executed because of their connection to Zai.

sentences.zh: 遣中官於萬年縣界黃臺鄉毀載祖及父母墳墓，斫棺棄柩，及私廟木主；

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs were sent to Huangtai Township on the border of Wannian County to destroy the tombs of Zai's ancestors and parents, chop open the coffins and cast out the coffin shells, and the spirit tablets of his private temple;
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs were sent to Huangtai Township in Wannian County to destroy the tombs of Zai's ancestors and parents, chop open the coffins and cast out the remains, and the spirit tablets of his private temple;

sentences.zh: 並載大寧裏、安仁裏二宅，充修百司廨宇。

translations.literal: and Zai's two mansions in Daning Lane and Anren Lane were taken to repair the office buildings of the hundred bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: and Zai's two mansions in Daning Lane and Anren Lane were seized to repair government office buildings.

sentences.zh: 以載籍沒鐘乳五百兩分賜中書門下御史臺五品已上、尚書省四品已上。

translations.literal: Five hundred liang of stalactite from Zai's confiscated property were distributed as gifts to officials of the fifth rank and above in the Secretariat, Chancellery, and Censorate, and the fourth rank and above in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred liang of stalactite from Zai's confiscated property were distributed among officials of the fifth rank and above in the Secretariat, Chancellery, and Censorate, and the fourth rank and above in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 附 王昂王昂者，出自戎旅，以軍功累遷河中尹，充河中節度使。

translations.literal: Appendix: Wang Ang. Wang Ang came from the military ranks; through military merit he was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Hezhong and served as military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Wang Ang. Wang Ang came from the military ranks; through military merit he rose to prefect of Hezhong and military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 貪縱不法，務於聚斂，以貨籓身。

translations.literal: Greedy and unrestrained in lawlessness, he devoted himself to amassing wealth and used goods to secure his post.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and lawless, he devoted himself to amassing wealth and used bribes to secure his post.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年正月，檢校刑部尚書知省事，改殿中少監。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yongtai he was acting minister of justice directing office affairs, then changed to vice director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yongtai (765) he was acting minister of justice directing office affairs, then became vice director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 元載秉政，與載深相結托。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai held power, Ang formed a deep bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai held power, Ang formed a deep alliance with him.

sentences.zh: 大曆五年六月，為江陵尹、兼御史大夫，充荊南節度觀察使，代衛伯玉。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Dali he became prefect of Jiangling, concurrent censor-in-chief, and Jingnan military commissioner and investigating commissioner, replacing Wei Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Dali (770) he became prefect of Jiangling, concurrent censor-in-chief, and Jingnan military commissioner and investigating commissioner, replacing Wei Boyu.

sentences.zh: 昂既行，伯玉諷大將楊𨨫等拒昂，乞留伯玉，詔許之。

translations.literal: After Ang had set out, Boyu prompted the great generals Yang Kui and others to resist Ang and beg that Boyu be kept; an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: After Ang had set out, Boyu prompted the great generals Yang Kui and others to resist him and petitioned that Boyu be retained; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 昂復檢校刑部尚書，知省事。

translations.literal: Ang again became acting minister of justice directing office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ang again became acting minister of justice directing office affairs.

sentences.zh: 專事奢靡，廣修第宅，多畜妓妾，以逞其誌。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to luxury, built mansions on a grand scale, and kept many courtesans and concubines to indulge his desires.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to luxury, built mansions on a grand scale, and kept many courtesans to indulge his desires.

sentences.zh: 在刑部，雖公務有程，昂耽徇私宴，連日不視曹事。

translations.literal: While in the Ministry of Justice, though public business had its schedule, Ang indulged in private feasts and for days on end did not attend to bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Ministry of Justice, though public business had its schedule, Ang indulged in private feasts and for days on end ignored bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 性貪吝，無愧茍得，乃鬻公廨園菜，收其錢以潤屋，甚為時論所醜。

translations.literal: By nature greedy and stingy, he felt no shame in grasping what he could; he even sold the vegetables from the government office garden and took the money to enrich his house—a thing much despised in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: By nature greedy and stingy, he felt no shame in grasping what he could; he even sold vegetables from the government office garden and used the money to enrich his house—a thing much despised in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 元載誅，貶連州刺史，遣中使監至萬州，過硤江，墜江而卒。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai was executed, Ang was demoted to prefect of Lianzhou; a palace envoy was sent to escort him under supervision to Wanzhou. Crossing the Xia River, he fell into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai was executed, Ang was demoted to prefect of Lianzhou; a palace envoy was sent to escort him under supervision to Wanzhou. Crossing the Xia River, he fell into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 附 李少良李少良者，以吏用，早從使幕，因職遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Appendix: Li Shaoliang. Li Shaoliang entered service as a clerk, early joined commissioners' staffs, and through office was promoted to attendant censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Li Shaoliang. Li Shaoliang entered service as a clerk, early joined commissioners' staffs, and was promoted to attendant censor in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 罷，遊京師，幹謁權貴。

translations.literal: When dismissed, he traveled in the capital and paid court to the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: When dismissed, he traveled in the capital and paid court to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 時元載專政，所居第宅崇侈，子弟縱橫，貨賄公行，士庶咸嫉之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zai monopolized government; his residence was lofty and extravagant, his sons and younger brothers ran rampant, and bribes were openly exchanged—scholars and commoners alike resented him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zai monopolized government; his residence was extravagant, his sons ran rampant, and bribes were openly exchanged—scholars and commoners alike resented him.

sentences.zh: 少良怨不見用，乘眾怒以抗疏上聞。

translations.literal: Shaoliang resented that he was not employed and, seizing on public anger, submitted a defiant memorial to reach the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoliang resented that he was not employed and, seizing on public anger, submitted a bold memorial to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 留少良於禁內客省，少良友人韋頌因至禁門訪少良，少良漏其言；

translations.literal: Shaoliang was detained in the inner palace guest office. His friend Wei Song came to the forbidden gate to visit Shaoliang, and Shaoliang leaked his words;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoliang was detained in the inner palace guest office. His friend Wei Song came to the forbidden gate to visit him, and Shaoliang leaked what had been said;

sentences.zh: 頌不慎密，遂為載備知之，乃奏少良狂妄，詔下御史臺訊鞫。

translations.literal: Song was not careful in secrecy, and Zai came to know everything. He then memorialized that Shaoliang was arrogant and mad; an edict ordered the Censorate to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Song was not careful to keep secrets, and Zai learned everything. He memorialized that Shaoliang was arrogant and mad; an edict ordered the Censorate to interrogate him.

sentences.zh: 是時御史大夫缺，載以張延賞為之，屬意焉。

translations.literal: At that time the post of censor-in-chief was vacant; Zai appointed Zhang Yanshang to it and placed his trust in him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the post of censor-in-chief was vacant; Zai appointed Zhang Yanshang to it and placed his trust in him.

sentences.zh: 少良以泄禁中奏議，制使陸珽同伏罪。

translations.literal: Shaoliang was convicted of leaking inner-palace memorial discussions; Commissioner Lu Ting confessed guilt along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoliang was convicted of leaking inner-palace memorial discussions; Commissioner Lu Ting confessed guilt along with him.

sentences.zh: 初，韋頌及珽俱與少良友善，與載子弟親黨款狎。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Song and Ting had both been friendly with Shaoliang and were on intimate terms with Zai's sons and close associates.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Song and Lu Ting had both been friendly with Shaoliang and were on intimate terms with Zai's sons and close associates.

sentences.zh: 頌得少良微旨，漏於載所親，遂達於載。

translations.literal: Song learned Shaoliang's subtle intent and leaked it to Zai's intimates, and it reached Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Song learned Shaoliang's intent and leaked it to Zai's intimates, and it reached Zai.

sentences.zh: 載密召珽問之，珽具白其狀及禁中語。

translations.literal: Zai secretly summoned Ting and questioned him; Ting fully reported the circumstances and the words from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zai secretly summoned Lu Ting and questioned him; Ting fully reported the circumstances and the words from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 載得之，奏於上前，上大怒，並付京兆府決殺。

translations.literal: When Zai learned of this, he memorialized before the emperor; the emperor was greatly angered and handed them all over to the metropolitan prefecture for execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai learned of this, he memorialized before the emperor; the emperor was greatly angered and handed them all over to the metropolitan prefecture for execution.

sentences.zh: 珽，國子司業善經之子也，少傳父業，頗通經史，性浮躁而疏，故及於累。

translations.literal: Ting was the son of Shanjing, vice director of the Directorate of Education. In youth he inherited his father's learning and was fairly versed in the classics and histories; his nature was frivolous and careless, and therefore he came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ting was the son of Shanjing, vice director of the Directorate of Education. In youth he inherited his father's learning and was fairly versed in the classics and histories; his nature was frivolous and careless, and therefore he came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 附 郇謨大曆中，元載弄權自恣，人皆惡之。

translations.literal: Appendix: Xun Mo. In the Dali era Yuan Zai manipulated power at will and all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Xun Mo. In the Dali era Yuan Zai manipulated power at will and all hated him.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，晉州男子郇謨以麻辮髮，持竹筐及葦席哭於東市。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, the man of Jin Prefecture Xun Mo, with hemp braided in his hair, held a bamboo basket and reed mat and wept at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year (773), a man of Jin Prefecture named Xun Mo, with hemp braided in his hair, held a bamboo basket and reed mat and wept at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，對曰：「有三十字請獻於上。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, he answered: "I have thirty characters to present to His Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: When people asked the reason, he answered: "I have thirty characters to present to His Majesty.

sentences.zh: 若無堪，便以竹筐貯屍，棄之於野。」

translations.literal: If they are not acceptable, I shall place my corpse in the bamboo basket and cast it in the wild."
translations.idiomatic: If they are not acceptable, I shall place my corpse in the bamboo basket and cast it in the wild."

sentences.zh: 京兆府以聞。

translations.literal: The metropolitan prefecture reported this.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan prefecture reported this.

sentences.zh: 上既召見，賜衣，館於禁內客省。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience, bestowed clothing, and lodged him in the inner palace guest office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him for audience, bestowed clothing, and lodged him in the inner palace guest office.

sentences.zh: 其獻三十字，各論一事。

translations.literal: The thirty characters he presented each discussed one matter.
translations.idiomatic: The thirty characters he presented each discussed one matter.

sentences.zh: 其要者：「團」字、「監」字。

translations.literal: The important ones were the character "Tuan" and the character "Jian."
translations.idiomatic: The important ones were the characters for "corps" and "supervisor."

sentences.zh: 團者，請罷諸州團練使；

translations.literal: "Tuan" meant: request abolition of the training-corps commissioners of all prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: "Corps" meant: request abolition of the training-corps commissioners of all prefectures;

sentences.zh: 監者，請罷諸道監軍使。

translations.literal: "Jian" meant: request abolition of the army-supervising commissioners of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: "Supervisor" meant: request abolition of the army-supervising commissioners of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 殿中御史楊護職居左巡，郇謨哭市，護不聞奏，上以為蔽匿，貶連州桂陽縣丞員外置。

translations.literal: Palace censor Yang Hu held the post of left patrol. When Xun Mo wept in the market, Hu did not hear and report it; the emperor considered this concealment and demoted him to supernumerary assistant magistrate of Guiyang County in Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Yang Hu held the post of left patrol. When Xun Mo wept in the market, Hu failed to report it; the emperor considered this concealment and demoted him to supernumerary assistant magistrate of Guiyang County in Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 元載當承寵得誌，每改張朝政，出於載手，中外共怒，當時歸咎於載，故少良封事於前，郇謨哭市於後。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai, when he received favor and achieved his ambition, altered court governance at every turn—all issuing from Zai's hand—and within and without the court all were angry. At the time blame was laid on Zai; hence Shaoliang's sealed memorial came first and Xun Mo's weeping in the market came after.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, once he received favor and achieved his ambition, altered court governance at every turn—all from his hand—and within and without the court all were angry. At the time blame was laid on Zai; hence Shaoliang's sealed memorial came first and Xun Mo's weeping in the market came after.

sentences.zh: 凡百有位，宜為明誡。

translations.literal: All who hold office should take this as a clear warning.
translations.idiomatic: All who hold office should take this as a clear warning.

sentences.zh: 王縉王縉，字夏卿，河中人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jin. Wang Jin, courtesy name Xiaqing, was a man of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin. Wang Jin, courtesy name Xiaqing, was a native of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少好學，與兄維早以文翰著名。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; with his elder brother Wei he was early famed for literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning; with his elder brother Wei he was early famed for literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 縉連應草澤及文辭清麗舉，累授侍御史、武部員外。

translations.literal: Jin successively passed the Hidden Talents and Elegant Literary Composition examinations and was repeatedly appointed attendant censor and vice director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Jin successively passed the Hidden Talents and Elegant Literary Composition examinations and was repeatedly appointed attendant censor and vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，選為太原少尹，與李光弼同守太原，功效謀略，眾所推先，加憲部侍郎，兼本官。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Lushan he was selected as vice prefect of Taiyuan; with Li Guangbi he jointly defended Taiyuan. In achievement and stratagem he was foremost among all; he was promoted to vice minister of justice while retaining his original post.
translations.idiomatic: During An Lushan's rebellion he was selected as vice prefect of Taiyuan; with Li Guangbi he jointly defended Taiyuan. In achievement and stratagem he was foremost among all; he was promoted to vice minister of justice while retaining his original post.

sentences.zh: 時兄維陷賊，受偽署，賊平，維付吏議，縉請以己官贖維之罪，特為減等。

translations.literal: At that time his elder brother Wei had fallen into the rebels' hands and accepted a false appointment. When the rebels were pacified, Wei was handed over to the judicial authorities for discussion. Jin asked to use his own office to redeem Wei's guilt, and a special reduction of penalty was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his elder brother Wei had fallen into rebel hands and accepted a false appointment. When the rebels were pacified, Wei was handed over for trial. Jin asked to use his own office to redeem Wei's guilt, and a special reduction of penalty was granted.

sentences.zh: 縉尋入拜國子祭酒，改鳳翔尹、秦隴州防禦使，歷工部侍郎、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jin soon entered the capital and was appointed chancellor of the Directorate of Education, then changed to prefect of Fengxiang and defense commissioner of Qin and Long prefectures; he served as vice minister of works and left regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jin soon entered the capital and was appointed chancellor of the Directorate of Education, then became prefect of Fengxiang and defense commissioner of Qin and Long prefectures; he served as vice minister of works and left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 撰《玄宗哀冊文》，時稱為工。

translations.literal: He composed the "Lament for Emperor Xuanzong," which at the time was praised as accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He composed the Lament for Emperor Xuanzong, which at the time was praised as accomplished.

sentences.zh: 改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 屬平殄史朝義，河朔未安，詔縉以本官河北宣慰，奉使稱旨。

translations.literal: When Shi Chaoyi was pacified and destroyed, the Hebei region was still unsettled; an edict appointed Jin with his existing office as Hebei pacification commissioner. His mission accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Chaoyi was destroyed, the Hebei region was still unsettled; an edict appointed Jin with his existing office as Hebei pacification commissioner. His mission accorded with the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，拜黃門侍郎、同平章事、太微宮使、弘文崇賢館大學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery, associate chief minister, commissioner of the Taiwei Palace, and grand academician of the Hongwen and Chongxian halls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangde (764) he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery, associate chief minister, commissioner of the Taiwei Palace, and grand academician of the Hongwen and Chongxian halls.

sentences.zh: 其年，河南副元帥李光弼薨於徐州，以縉為侍中、持節都統河南、淮西、山南東道諸節度行營事。

translations.literal: That same year the deputy commander-in-chief of Henan Li Guangbi died at Xuzhou; Jin was appointed palace attendant and commissioner with credentials overseeing all Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuit military headquarters and field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Henan Li Guangbi died at Xuzhou; Jin was appointed palace attendant and commissioner with credentials overseeing all Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuit military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 縉懇讓侍中，從之，加上柱國，兼東都留守。

translations.literal: Jin earnestly declined the post of palace attendant; this was granted. He was given the supreme pillar of state rank and made concurrent Eastern Capital Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Jin earnestly declined the post of palace attendant; this was granted. He was given the supreme pillar of state rank and made concurrent protector of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷河南副元帥，請減軍資錢四十萬貫修東都殿宇。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to deputy commander-in-chief of Henan and requested that four hundred thousand strings of military funds be reduced to repair the halls of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to deputy commander-in-chief of Henan and requested that four hundred thousand strings of military funds be diverted to repair the halls of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 大曆三年，幽州節度使李懷仙死，以縉領幽州、盧龍節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali the Youzhou military commissioner Li Huaixian died; Jin was put in charge of Youzhou and Lulong military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dali (768) the Youzhou military commissioner Li Huaixian died; Jin was put in charge of the Youzhou and Lulong military commissions.

sentences.zh: 縉赴鎮而還，委政於燕將朱希彩。

translations.literal: Jin went to his post and returned, entrusting government to the Yan general Zhu Xicai.
translations.idiomatic: Jin went to his post and returned, entrusting government to the Yan general Zhu Xicai.

sentences.zh: 又屬河東節度辛雲京卒，遂兼太原尹、北都留守、河東節度營田觀察等使。

translations.literal: It also happened that Hedong military commissioner Xin Yunjing died; Jin was then made concurrent prefect of Taiyuan, northern capital protector, and Hedong military commissioner, garrison-field commissioner, and investigating commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: It also happened that Hedong military commissioner Xin Yunjing died; Jin was then made concurrent prefect of Taiyuan, northern capital protector, and Hedong military commissioner, garrison-field commissioner, and investigating commissioner.

sentences.zh: 縉又讓河南副元帥、東都留守，從之。

translations.literal: Jin again declined the posts of deputy commander-in-chief of Henan and Eastern Capital Protector; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin again declined the posts of deputy commander-in-chief of Henan and protector of the Eastern Capital; this was granted.

sentences.zh: 太原舊將王無縱、張奉璋等恃功，且以縉儒者易之，每事多違約束。

translations.literal: The old Taiyuan generals Wang Wuzong, Zhang Fengzhang, and others relied on their merit and, considering Jin a scholar easy to deal with, often violated regulations in their affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The old Taiyuan generals Wang Wuzong, Zhang Fengzhang, and others relied on their merit and, considering Jin a scholar easy to deal with, often violated regulations.

sentences.zh: 縉一朝悉召斬之，將校股栗。

translations.literal: Jin summoned them all in one morning and had them beheaded; officers and generals trembled in their thighs.
translations.idiomatic: Jin summoned them all in one morning and had them beheaded; officers and generals trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 二歲，罷河東歸朝，授門下侍郎、中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: After two years he was removed from Hedong and returned to court, appointed vice director of the Chancellery and chief minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was removed from Hedong and returned to court, appointed vice director of the Chancellery and chief minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時元載用事，縉卑附之，不敢與忤，然恃才與老，多所傲忽。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zai held power; Jin humbled himself and attached to him, not daring to oppose him, yet relying on his talent and age he was often arrogant and neglectful.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zai held power; Jin humbled himself and attached to him, not daring to oppose him, yet relying on his talent and age he was often arrogant and dismissive.

sentences.zh: 載所不悅，心雖希載旨，然以言辭淩詬，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: What Zai did not like, though in heart he wished to please Zai's intent, he still insulted with words and showed no fear or restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Though in heart he wished to please Zai, he still insulted with words whatever Zai disliked and showed no fear or restraint.

sentences.zh: 時京兆尹黎幹者，戎州人也，數論事，載甚病之，而力不能去也。

translations.literal: At that time the metropolitan prefect Li Gan was a man of Rong Prefecture who often discussed affairs; Zai greatly resented this but lacked the power to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the metropolitan prefect Li Gan was a man of Rong Prefecture who often discussed affairs; Zai greatly resented this but lacked the power to remove him.

sentences.zh: 幹嘗白事於縉，縉曰：「尹，南方君子也，安知朝禮！」

translations.literal: Gan once reported affairs to Jin; Jin said: "Prefect, you are a southern gentleman—how would you know court ritual!"
translations.idiomatic: Gan once reported affairs to Jin; Jin said: "Prefect, you are a southern gentleman—how would you know court ritual!"

sentences.zh: 其慢而侮人，率如此類。

translations.literal: His arrogance and insult to others were generally of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His arrogance and insult to others were generally of this sort.

sentences.zh: 縉弟兄奉佛，不茹葷血，縉晚年尤甚。

translations.literal: Jin and his brothers observed Buddhism and did not eat meat or blood; in his later years Jin was especially strict in this.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and his brothers observed Buddhism and did not eat meat; in his later years Jin was especially strict in this.

sentences.zh: 與杜鴻漸舍財造寺無限極。

translations.literal: With Du Hongjian he gave wealth to build temples without limit.
translations.idiomatic: With Du Hongjian he gave wealth to build temples without limit.

sentences.zh: 妻李氏卒，舍道政里第為寺，為之追福，奏其額曰寶應，度僧三十人住持。

translations.literal: When his wife Lady Li died, he gave his mansion in Daozheng Lane to become a temple, seeking merit for her, memorialized that its plaque read Baoying, and ordained thirty monks to reside there as abbots.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife Lady Li died, he gave his mansion in Daozheng Lane to become a temple, seeking merit for her, memorialized that its plaque read Baoying, and ordained thirty monks to reside there as abbots.

sentences.zh: 每節度觀察使入朝，必延至寶應寺，諷令施財，助己修繕。

translations.literal: Whenever military and investigating commissioners came to court, he always invited them to Baoying Temple and hinted that they should give wealth to help his own repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever military and investigating commissioners came to court, he always invited them to Baoying Temple and hinted that they should give wealth to help his own repairs.

sentences.zh: 初，代宗喜祠祀，未甚重佛，而元載、杜鴻漸與縉喜飯僧徒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Daizong delighted in sacrifices and did not greatly esteem Buddhism, but Yuan Zai, Du Hongjian, and Jin delighted in feeding monks.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Daizong delighted in sacrifices and did not greatly esteem Buddhism, but Yuan Zai, Du Hongjian, and Jin delighted in feeding monks.

sentences.zh: 代宗嘗問以福業報應事，載等因而啟奏，代宗由是奉之過當，嘗令僧百餘人於宮中陳設佛像，經行念誦，謂之內道場。

translations.literal: Daizong once asked about matters of karmic merit and retribution; Zai and the others thereupon memorialized, and Daizong from this honored it excessively. He once ordered more than a hundred monks within the palace to set out Buddha images, walk in procession chanting sutras—this was called the inner dharma hall.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong once asked about karmic merit and retribution; Zai and the others thereupon memorialized, and Daizong from this honored Buddhism excessively. He once ordered more than a hundred monks within the palace to set out Buddha images and walk in procession chanting sutras—this was called the inner dharma hall.

sentences.zh: 其飲膳之厚，窮極珍異，出入乘廄焉，度支具廩給。

translations.literal: Their food and drink were lavish to the utmost in rare delicacies; they went in and out riding the imperial stables, and the Bureau of Revenue supplied their grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Their food and drink were lavish to the utmost in rare delicacies; they went in and out riding imperial horses, and the Bureau of Revenue supplied their grain rations.

sentences.zh: 每西蕃入寇，必令群僧講誦《仁王經》，以攘虜寇。

translations.literal: Whenever the western Tibetans invaded, he always ordered the assembly of monks to lecture and chant the Humane Kings Sutra to repel the barbarian invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the western Tibetans invaded, he always ordered monks to lecture and chant the Humane Kings Sutra to repel the invaders.

sentences.zh: 茍幸其退，則橫加錫賜。

translations.literal: If by chance they withdrew, he then lavished rewards upon them.
translations.idiomatic: If by chance they withdrew, he then lavished rewards upon the monks.

sentences.zh: 胡僧不空，官至卿監，封國公，通籍禁中，勢移公卿，爭權擅威，日相淩奪。

translations.literal: The foreign monk Bukong rose to ministerial and supervisory rank, was enfeoffed as duke of state, had registry in the forbidden palace, shifted power against the chief ministers, and contended for authority and monopolized prestige, daily encroaching upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign monk Amoghavajra rose to ministerial rank, was enfeoffed as duke of state, had registry in the forbidden palace, shifted power against the chief ministers, and contended for authority daily, encroaching upon one another.

sentences.zh: 凡京畿之豐田美利，多歸於寺觀，吏不能制。

translations.literal: All the rich fields and fine profits of the capital region mostly passed to temples and monasteries; officials could not control this.
translations.idiomatic: All the rich fields and fine profits of the capital region mostly passed to temples and monasteries; officials could not control this.

sentences.zh: 僧之徒侶，雖有贓奸畜亂，敗戮相繼，而代宗信心不易，乃詔天下官吏不得箠曳僧尼。

translations.literal: Though among the monks' companions there were those guilty of corruption, treachery, and breeding disorder, with ruin and execution following one after another, Daizong's faith did not change; he then issued an edict that officials throughout the realm must not flog or drag monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: Though among the monks there were those guilty of corruption and breeding disorder, with ruin and execution following one after another, Daizong's faith did not change; he issued an edict that officials throughout the realm must not flog or drag monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 又見縉等施財立寺，窮極瑰麗，每對揚啟沃，必以業果為證。

translations.literal: He also saw Jin and the others give wealth to establish temples of utmost splendor; whenever they addressed and instructed him in audience, they always cited karmic cause and effect as proof.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw Jin and the others give wealth to establish temples of utmost splendor; whenever they addressed him in audience, they always cited karmic cause and effect as proof.

sentences.zh: 以為國家慶祚靈長，皆福報所資，業力已定，雖小有患難，不足道也。

translations.literal: They held that the state's felicitous fortune and spiritual longevity all depended on karmic reward; once karmic power was fixed, though there were minor calamities and difficulties, these were not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: They held that the state's felicitous fortune and longevity all depended on karmic reward; once karmic power was fixed, though there were minor calamities, these were not worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 故祿山、思明毒亂方熾，而皆有子禍。

translations.literal: Thus though Lushan and Siming's poisonous rebellion was at its height, both suffered calamity through their sons.
translations.idiomatic: Thus though Lushan and Siming's rebellion was at its height, both suffered calamity through their sons.

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩將亂而死；

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en was about to rebel and died;
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en was about to rebel and died;

sentences.zh: 西戎犯闕，未擊而退。

translations.literal: the western Rong violated the palace precincts and withdrew without being struck.
translations.idiomatic: the western barbarians violated the palace precincts and withdrew without being struck.

sentences.zh: 此皆非人事之明徵也。

translations.literal: These were none of them clear signs from human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: These were none of them clear signs from human affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 帝信之愈甚。

translations.literal: The emperor believed this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed this all the more.

sentences.zh: 公卿大臣既掛以業報，則人事棄而不修，故大曆刑政，日以陵遲，有由然也。

translations.literal: Once the chief ministers and high officials were hung upon karmic retribution, human affairs were abandoned and not maintained; hence under Dali, punishment and governance daily declined—there was reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: Once the chief ministers had been hung upon karmic retribution, human affairs were neglected and left untended; under the Dali era, law and governance steadily decayed—and there was good reason for it.

sentences.zh: 五臺山有金閣寺，鑄銅為瓦，塗金於上，照耀山谷，計錢巨億萬。

translations.literal: On Wutai Mountain was Jinge Temple; copper was cast into tiles and gilded atop them, shining upon the valleys—the cost reckoned in hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: On Wutai Mountain stood Jinge Temple, whose roof tiles were cast in copper and gilded until they blazed across the valleys—a sum reckoned in the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 縉為宰相，給中書符牒，令臺山僧數十人分行郡縣，聚徒講說，以求貨利。

translations.literal: Jin being chief minister, issued Zhongshu tally-documents, ordering several dozen Mount Tai monks to travel separately through prefectures and counties, gathering followers to preach, seeking profit.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Jin issued tally-documents from the Secretariat ordering several dozen Wutai monks to fan out through the prefectures and counties, gathering disciples to preach for profit.

sentences.zh: 代宗七月望日於內道場造盂蘭盆，飾以金翠，所費百萬。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, Daizong made an Ullambana feast at the Inner Chapel, adorned with gold and kingfisher ornaments—the cost a million.
translations.idiomatic: On the full moon of the seventh month, Daizong held an Ullambana feast in the Inner Chapel, adorned with gold and kingfisher ornaments at a cost of a million.

sentences.zh: 又設高祖已下七聖神座，備幡節、龍傘、衣裳之制，各書尊號於幡上以識之，舁出內，陳於寺觀。

translations.literal: He also set up spirit seats for the seven sages from Gaozu downward, fully provisioned with banners, insignia, dragon umbrellas, and robes as prescribed; each honorific title was written on banners for identification, then carried out from within the palace and displayed at temples and monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up spirit tablets for the seven imperial ancestors from Gaozu downward, complete with banners, insignia, dragon umbrellas, and ceremonial robes; each honorific title was written on a banner for identification, then borne out from the palace and displayed at temples and monasteries.

sentences.zh: 是日，排儀仗，百僚序立於光順門以俟之，幡花鼓舞，迎呼道路。

translations.literal: That day ceremonial guards were arrayed; the hundred officials stood in order at Guangshun Gate to await them; banner flowers and drum dances greeted and shouted along the roads.
