translations.idiomatic: That day ceremonial guards were deployed and the hundred officials lined up in order at Guangshun Gate to receive them; banners, flowers, and drums welcomed them with shouts all along the road.

sentences.zh: 歲以為常，而識者嗤其不典，其傷教之源始於縉也。

translations.literal: Year after year this became routine, yet the discerning mocked it as uncanonical; the source of harm to the teachings began with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year this became routine, yet the discerning mocked it as uncanonical—the source of injury to the faith began with Jin.

sentences.zh: 李氏，初為左丞韋濟妻，濟卒，奔縉。

translations.literal: Lady Li had first been wife to Left Vice Director Wei Ji; when Ji died, she fled to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li had first been the wife of Left Vice Director Wei Ji; when Ji died, she went to Jin.

sentences.zh: 縉嬖之，冒稱為妻，實妾也。

translations.literal: Jin favored her, falsely claiming her as wife—she was in fact a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Jin favored her and falsely claimed she was his wife, though she was in fact a concubine.

sentences.zh: 又縱弟妹女尼等廣納財賄，貪猥之跡如市賈焉。

translations.literal: He also allowed his siblings, sisters, and nun relatives to take bribes widely; their greedy, base conduct resembled market traders.
translations.idiomatic: He also allowed his siblings, sisters, and nun relatives to take bribes on a wide scale; their greedy, base conduct was like that of market traders.

sentences.zh: 元載得罪，縉連坐貶括州刺史，移處州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai fell from grace, Jin was implicated and demoted to prefect of Kuozhou, then transferred to prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai fell from grace, Jin was implicated and demoted to prefect of Kuozhou, then transferred to prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年，除太子賓客，留司東都。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dali he was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent and remained on duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 14 (779) he was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent and remained on duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 建中二年十二月卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Jianzhong he died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of Jianzhong 2 (781), aged eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 楊炎楊炎，字公南，鳳翔人。

translations.literal: Yang Yan. Yang Yan, courtesy name Gongnan, was a man of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan. Yang Yan, courtesy name Gongnan, was a native of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖大寶，武德初為龍門令，劉武周陷晉、絳，攻之不降，城破被害，褒贈全節侯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dabao, at the beginning of Wude served as magistrate of Longmen; when Liu Wuzhou seized Jin and Jiang, he attacked but would not surrender; when the city fell he was killed, and posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Quanjie.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dabao served as magistrate of Longmen at the beginning of Wude (618); when Liu Wuzhou seized Jin and Jiang, Dabao held out and refused to surrender; when the city fell he was killed and was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Quanjie.

sentences.zh: 祖哲，以孝行有異，旌其門閭。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhe, for extraordinary filial conduct, had his gate and lane honored with a commemorative marker.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhe, for extraordinary filial conduct, had his gate and lane honored with a commemorative marker.

sentences.zh: 父播，登進士第，隱居不仕，玄宗徵為諫議大夫，棄官就養，亦以孝行禎祥，表其門閭。

translations.literal: His father Bo passed the jinshi examination, lived in seclusion and did not serve; Xuanzong summoned him as Remonstrance Grandee, but he abandoned office to go and support his parents; he too, for filial conduct and auspicious signs, had his gate and lane marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bo passed the jinshi examination and lived in seclusion without taking office; Xuanzong summoned him as Remonstrance Grandee, but he resigned to care for his parents; he too, for filial conduct and auspicious omens, had his gate and lane marked with honor.

sentences.zh: 肅宗就加散騎常侍，賜號玄靖先生，名在《逸人傳》。

translations.literal: Suzong thereupon added him as Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and bestowed the title Master Xuanjing; his name appears in the Biographies of Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong thereupon promoted him to Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and bestowed the title Master Xuanjing; his name appears in the Biographies of Recluses.

sentences.zh: 炎美鬚眉，風骨峻峙，文藻雄麗，汧、隴之間，號為小楊山人。

translations.literal: Yan had fine beard and brows, stern bearing and lofty presence, and writing of heroic splendor; between Qian and Long he was called the Lesser Yang Mountain Man.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had fine beard and brows, a stern and commanding presence, and writing of heroic splendor; between Qian and Long he was known as the Lesser Yang Mountain Man.

sentences.zh: 釋褐辟河西節度掌書記。

translations.literal: Upon leaving student status he was recruited as secretary to the Hexi military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering official life he was recruited as secretary to the Hexi military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 神烏令李大簡嘗因醉辱炎，至是與炎同幕，率左右反接之，鐵棒撾之二百，流血被地，幾死。

translations.literal: Li Dajian, magistrate of Shenwu, had once insulted Yan while drunk; now serving on the same staff, he led his attendants to bind Yan's arms behind him and beat him two hundred blows with an iron rod—blood covered the ground and he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dajian, magistrate of Shenwu, had once insulted Yan while drunk; now serving on the same staff, he had his attendants bind Yan's arms behind his back and beat him two hundred blows with an iron rod—blood covered the ground and he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 節度使呂崇賁愛其才，不之責。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Lü Chongben valued his talent and did not hold him accountable.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner Lü Chongben valued his talent and did not hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 後副元帥李光弼奏為判官，不應，徵拜起居舍人，辭祿就養岐下。

translations.literal: Later the deputy commander Li Guangbi memorialized to appoint him judge; he did not accept. He was summoned and appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent, but declined the salary to go and support his parents below Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later the deputy commander Li Guangbi recommended him as judge, but he declined. Summoned as Attendant of the Heir Apparent, he resigned his salary to care for his parents in the Qi region.

sentences.zh: 丁憂，廬於墓前，號泣不絕聲，有紫芝白雀之祥，又表其門閭。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning obligations he built a hut before the tomb and wailed without cease; there were auspicious signs of purple fungus and white sparrows, and again his gate and lane were marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he built a hut before the tomb and wailed without cease; auspicious signs appeared in the form of purple fungus and white sparrows, and again his gate and lane were marked with honor.

sentences.zh: 孝著三代，門樹六闕，古未有也。

translations.literal: Filial renown spanning three generations, six commemorative towers at the gate—never before in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Filial renown spanning three generations and six commemorative towers at the gate—unprecedented in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 服闋久之，起為司勛員外郎，改兵部，轉禮部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Long after mourning ended he was recalled as vice director in the Bureau of Merits, transferred to the Ministry of War, then promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Long after mourning ended he was recalled as vice director in the Bureau of Merits, transferred to the Ministry of War, then promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，與常袞並掌綸誥，袞長於除書，炎善為德音，自開元已來，言詔制之美者，時稱常、楊焉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Drafter; with Chang Gao he jointly handled edicts and proclamations—Gao excelled at appointment documents, Yan was skilled at benevolent pronouncements; from Kaiyuan onward, when speaking of the beauty of edicts and decrees, the age called them Chang and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat Drafter and, with Chang Gao, jointly handled edicts and proclamations—Gao excelled at appointment documents, Yan at benevolent pronouncements; from Kaiyuan onward, when people spoke of the finest edicts and decrees, they spoke of Chang and Yang.

sentences.zh: 炎樂賢下士，以汲引為己任，人士歸之。

translations.literal: Yan delighted in honoring the worthy and deferring to men of talent, taking advancement of others as his own charge; scholars and officials rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan delighted in honoring the worthy and deferring to men of talent, making the advancement of others his personal mission; scholars and officials rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《李楷洛碑》，辭甚工，文士莫不成誦之。

translations.literal: He once composed the Stele for Li Kailuo; the wording was extremely polished, and literary men all memorized it by heart.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed the Stele for Li Kailuo; the wording was exquisitely crafted, and literary men all memorized it by heart.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel and took charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 元載自作相，常選擢朝士有文學才望者一人厚遇之，將以代己。

translations.literal: After Yuan Zai himself became chief minister, he regularly selected and promoted one court scholar of literary talent and reputation, treating him generously, intending to have him succeed himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Zai himself became chief minister, he regularly selected one court scholar of literary talent and reputation, treated him generously, and intended him as his successor.

sentences.zh: 初，引禮部郎中劉單；

translations.literal: At first he brought forward Liu Dan, director in the Ministry of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: At first he brought forward Liu Dan, director in the Ministry of Rites;

sentences.zh: 單卒，引吏部侍郎薛邕，邕貶，又引炎。

translations.literal: when Dan died, he brought forward Xue Yong, vice minister of personnel; when Yong was demoted, he brought forward Yan.
translations.idiomatic: when Dan died, he brought forward Xue Yong, vice minister of personnel; when Yong was demoted, he brought forward Yan.

sentences.zh: 載親重炎，無與為比。

translations.literal: Zai personally favored Yan above all comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Zai personally favored Yan as none other.

sentences.zh: 載敗，坐貶道州司馬。

translations.literal: When Zai fell, Yan was implicated and demoted to military adjutant of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai fell, Yan was implicated and demoted to military adjutant of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，議用宰相，崔祐甫薦炎有文學器用，上亦自聞其名，拜銀青光祿大夫、門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, chief ministers were under discussion; Cui Youfu recommended Yan for literary talent and practical capacity; the emperor too had heard his name himself; he was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Associate Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong took the throne and chief ministers were under discussion, Cui Youfu recommended Yan for literary talent and practical capacity; the emperor too had heard of him and appointed him Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 炎有風儀，博以文學，早負時稱，天下翕然，望為賢相。

translations.literal: Yan had dignified bearing, was broadly accomplished in letters, had early borne the age's praise; all under Heaven converged in hope that he would be a worthy chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had dignified bearing and broad literary accomplishment; long celebrated, he drew the hopes of the realm that he would prove a worthy chief minister.

sentences.zh: 初，國家舊制，天下財賦皆納於左藏庫，而太府四時以數聞，尚書比部覆其出入，上下相轄，無失遺。

translations.literal: Formerly, by the state's old system, all revenue and levies under Heaven were paid into the Left Treasury; the Grand Storehouse reported the figures each season, the Ministry of Revenue's Audit Bureau reviewed receipts and disbursements, upper and lower mutually checked one another, and nothing was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, by the state's old system, all revenue under Heaven was paid into the Left Treasury; the Grand Storehouse reported the figures each season, the Ministry of Revenue's Audit Bureau reviewed receipts and disbursements, and upper and lower offices checked one another so that nothing was lost.

sentences.zh: 及第五琦為度支、鹽鐵使，京師多豪將，求取無節，琦不能禁，乃悉以租賦進入大盈內庫，以中人主之意，天子以取給為便，故不復出。

translations.literal: When Diwu Qi became commissioner of revenue and salt and iron, the capital had many powerful generals whose demands were unbounded; Qi could not restrain them, so he had all rent and levies forwarded into the Great Abundance Inner Treasury to satisfy the eunuchs who controlled the emperor's mind; the Son of Heaven found it convenient to draw supplies from there, and so they were never returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Diwu Qi became commissioner of revenue and salt and iron, the capital had many powerful generals whose demands were unbounded; unable to restrain them, Qi had all rent and levies forwarded into the Great Abundance Inner Treasury to satisfy the eunuchs who controlled the emperor's mind; the Son of Heaven found it convenient to draw supplies from there, and so they were never returned.

sentences.zh: 是以天下公賦，為人君私藏，有司不得窺其多少，國用不能計其贏縮，殆二十年矣。

translations.literal: Thus the public levies of all under Heaven became the monarch's private store; responsible officials could not glimpse how much there was; state expenditure could not calculate surplus or deficit—nearly twenty years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the public levies of the realm became the monarch's private hoard; responsible officials could not see how much there was, and state expenditure could not be measured for surplus or deficit—nearly twenty years had passed.

sentences.zh: 中官以冗名持簿書，領其事者三百人，皆奉給其間，連結根固不可動。

translations.literal: Eunuchs held the ledgers under supernumerary titles; three hundred men managed the affair, all drawing salaries from it—their connections rooted deep and immovable.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs held the ledgers under supernumerary titles; three hundred men managed the affair, all drawing salaries from it—their connections were deeply rooted and immovable.

sentences.zh: 及炎作相，頓首於上前，論之曰：「夫財賦，邦國之大本，生人之喉命，天下理亂輕重皆由焉。

translations.literal: When Yan became chief minister, he bowed his head to the ground before the emperor and argued, saying: "Revenue and levies are the great foundation of the state, the throat and life of the people; the weight of order and disorder under Heaven all depend upon them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan became chief minister, he bowed his head before the emperor and argued: "Revenue and levies are the great foundation of the state, the very life-blood of the people; the weight of order and disorder under Heaven all depend upon them.

sentences.zh: 是以前代歷選重臣主之，猶懼不集，往往覆敗，大計一失，則天下動搖。

translations.literal: Hence former ages repeatedly selected weighty ministers to manage them, yet still feared failure; often they collapsed in ruin—once the great plan was lost, all under Heaven was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Hence former ages repeatedly selected weighty ministers to manage them, yet still feared failure; often they collapsed in ruin—once the great plan was lost, the realm was shaken.

sentences.zh: 先朝權制，中人領其職，以五尺宦豎操邦之本，豐儉盈虛，雖大臣不得知，則無以計天下利害。

translations.literal: The previous court's expedient arrangement had eunuchs hold this charge—a five-foot palace attendant wielding the state's foundation; whether full or lean, surplus or deficit, even great ministers could not know—then there was no way to calculate the realm's benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: The previous court's expedient arrangement had eunuchs hold this charge—a five-foot palace attendant wielding the state's foundation; whether revenues were full or lean, surplus or deficit, even great ministers could not know—then there was no way to calculate the realm's benefit and harm.

sentences.zh: 臣愚待罪宰輔，陛下至德，惟人是恤，參校蠹弊，無斯之甚。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant, bearing guilt as chief councilor, finds Your Majesty's supreme virtue cares for the people; comparing and examining corrupt abuses, none is graver than this.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant, bearing guilt as chief councilor, finds Your Majesty's supreme virtue cares for the people; comparing corrupt abuses, none is graver than this.

sentences.zh: 請出之以歸有司，度宮中經費一歲幾何，量數奉入，不敢虧用。

translations.literal: I request that it be brought out and returned to the responsible offices; estimate how much the palace requires for a year's expenses, measure out that amount for delivery, and dare not fall short in use.
translations.idiomatic: I request that it be brought out and returned to the responsible offices; estimate how much the palace requires for a year's expenses, measure out that amount for delivery, and dare not fall short in use.

sentences.zh: 如此，然後可以議政。

translations.literal: Only thus can governance then be deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can governance be properly deliberated.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察焉。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty examine this.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty examine this.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「凡財賦皆歸左藏庫，一用舊式，每歲於數中量進三五十萬入大盈，而度支先以其全數聞。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "All revenue and levies shall return to the Left Treasury, following the old form entirely; each year from the total figures a measured amount of three to five hundred thousand shall be forwarded into Great Abundance, while the Revenue Commission first reports the full amount."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "All revenue and levies shall return to the Left Treasury, following the old form entirely; each year a measured amount of three to five hundred thousand shall be forwarded into Great Abundance, while the Revenue Commission first reports the full amount.

sentences.zh: 炎以片言移人主意，議者以為難，中外稱之。

translations.literal: Yan with a few words shifted the ruler's intent; deliberators considered it difficult; within and without the court praised it.
translations.idiomatic: With a few words Yan shifted the ruler's intent; deliberators considered it a difficult achievement, and praise came from within and without the court.

sentences.zh: 初定令式，國家有租賦庸調之法。

translations.literal: When statutes and forms were first fixed, the state had the system of rent, levy, corvée, and diao tax.
translations.idiomatic: When statutes and forms were first fixed, the state had the system of rent, levy, corvée, and diao tax.

sentences.zh: 開元中，玄宗修道德，以寬仁為理本，故不為版籍之書，人戶浸溢，堤防不禁。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, Xuanzong cultivated virtue and took leniency and benevolence as the root of governance; hence he did not compile household registers; population overflowed and dikes and barriers were not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan, Xuanzong cultivated virtue and took leniency and benevolence as the root of governance; hence he did not compile household registers; the population swelled unchecked and regulatory barriers were not enforced.

sentences.zh: 丁口轉死，非舊名矣；

translations.literal: Household members died or moved away—they were no longer the old names;
translations.idiomatic: Household members died or moved away—they were no longer the names on the old registers;

sentences.zh: 田畝移換，非舊額矣；

translations.literal: fields and mu changed hands—they were no longer the old quotas;
translations.idiomatic: fields changed hands—they no longer matched the old quotas;

sentences.zh: 貧富升降，非舊第矣。

translations.literal: rich and poor rose and fell—they were no longer the old ranks.
translations.idiomatic: rich and poor rose and fell—they no longer matched the old ranks.

sentences.zh: 戶部徒以空文總其故書，蓋得非當時之實。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue merely summed the old documents in empty text—hardly obtaining the reality of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue merely tallied the old documents on paper—hardly reflecting the reality of the time.

sentences.zh: 舊制，人丁戍邊者，蠲其租庸，六歲免歸。

translations.literal: By the old system, when men were garrisoned on the frontier, their rent and corvée were remitted; after six years they were exempted and returned.
translations.idiomatic: By the old system, when men were garrisoned on the frontier, their rent and corvée were remitted; after six years they were exempted and returned home.

sentences.zh: 玄宗方事夷狄，戍者多死不返，邊將怙寵而諱，不以死申，故其貫籍之名不除。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was then engaged with the barbarians; many garrison soldiers died and did not return; frontier generals, relying on favor, concealed this and did not report deaths, so their names on the permanent registers were not removed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong was then engaged with the barbarians; many garrison soldiers died and did not return; frontier generals, relying on imperial favor, concealed this and did not report deaths, so their names on the permanent registers were not removed.

sentences.zh: 至天寶中，王鉷為戶口使，方務聚斂，以丁籍且存，則丁身焉往，是隱課而不出耳。

translations.literal: By Tianbao, Wang Hong served as household commissioner, then bent on accumulation; since the household register still listed the men, where had the men themselves gone?—this was concealed taxation not paid.
translations.idiomatic: By Tianbao, Wang Hong served as household commissioner and was bent on accumulation; since the household register still listed the men, where had the men themselves gone?—this was concealed taxation not paid.

sentences.zh: 遂案舊籍，計除六年之外，積徵其家三十年租庸。

translations.literal: He then examined the old registers, calculating beyond the six-year exemption, and cumulatively levied thirty years of rent and corvée from their families.
translations.idiomatic: He then examined the old registers and, beyond the six-year exemption, cumulatively levied thirty years of rent and corvée from their families.

sentences.zh: 天下之人苦而無告，則租庸之法弊久矣。

translations.literal: The people of all under Heaven suffered with none to whom they could appeal—thus the rent-and-corvée system had long been broken.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the realm suffered with none to whom they could appeal—the rent-and-corvée system had long been broken.

sentences.zh: 迨至德之後，天下兵起，始以兵役，因之饑癘，徵求運輸，百役並作，人戶雕耗，版圖空虛。

translations.literal: By the time after Zhide, warfare arose throughout the realm; first came military service, then famine and pestilence, requisitions and transport—all corvées arose together; households were depleted and the territorial registers emptied.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide, warfare arose throughout the realm; first came military service, then famine and pestilence, requisitions and transport—all corvées arose together; households were depleted and the territorial registers emptied.

sentences.zh: 軍國之用，仰給於度支、轉運二使；

translations.literal: Expenditure for army and state depended on the two commissioners of revenue and transport;
translations.idiomatic: Expenditure for army and state depended on the two commissioners of revenue and transport;

sentences.zh: 四方征鎮，又自給於節度、都團練使。

translations.literal: the military garrisons of the four directions likewise supplied themselves through military commissioners and grand training-corps commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: the military garrisons of the four directions likewise supplied themselves through military commissioners and grand training-corps commissioners.

sentences.zh: 賦斂之司數四，而莫相統攝，於是綱目大壞，朝廷不能覆諸使，諸使不能覆諸州，四方貢獻，悉入內庫。

translations.literal: There were as many as four levying offices, yet none supervised one another; thus the whole structure was greatly broken—the court could not oversee the commissioners, the commissioners could not oversee the prefectures; tribute from the four directions all entered the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: There were as many as four levying offices, yet none supervised one another; thus the whole structure collapsed—the court could not oversee the commissioners, the commissioners could not oversee the prefectures; tribute from the four directions all entered the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 權臣猾吏，因緣為奸，或公托進獻，私為贓盜者動萬萬計。

translations.literal: Powerful ministers and crafty officials seized the opportunity for villainy; some publicly offered tribute while privately embezzling—amounts reaching tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful ministers and crafty officials seized the opportunity for villainy; some publicly offered tribute while privately embezzling—amounts reaching tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 河南、山東、荊襄、劍南有重兵處，皆厚自奉養，王賦所入無幾。

translations.literal: In Henan, Shandong, Jingxiang, and Jiannan, wherever heavy troops were stationed, all richly maintained themselves; what entered the royal levies was trifling.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, Shandong, Jingxiang, and Jiannan, wherever heavy troops were stationed, all richly maintained themselves; little reached the royal levies.

sentences.zh: 吏職之名，隨人署置；

translations.literal: The names of official posts were assigned at will;
translations.idiomatic: The names of official posts were assigned at will;

sentences.zh: 俸給厚薄，由其增損。

translations.literal: the thickness or thinness of salaries depended on their increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: salaries were raised or cut at their discretion.

sentences.zh: 故科斂之名凡數百，廢者不削，重者不去，新舊仍積，不知其涯。

translations.literal: Hence the names of exactions numbered in the hundreds; abolished ones were not cut away, heavy ones were not removed; old and new still accumulated—no knowing their limit.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the names of exactions numbered in the hundreds; abolished ones were not cut away, heavy ones were not removed; old and new levies piled up with no end in sight.

sentences.zh: 百姓受命而供之，瀝膏血，鬻親愛，旬輸月送無休息。

translations.literal: The common people received orders and supplied them—draining marrow and blood, selling beloved kin, delivering every ten days and every month without rest.
translations.idiomatic: The common people received orders and supplied them—draining their marrow and blood, selling beloved kin, delivering every ten days and every month without rest.

sentences.zh: 吏因其苛，蠶食千人。

translations.literal: Officials, relying on this harshness, gnawed away at the people like silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, relying on this harshness, gnawed away at the people like silkworms.

sentences.zh: 凡富人多丁者，率為官為僧，以色役免；

translations.literal: Generally the rich with many sons mostly became officials or monks, exempted through corvée by status;
translations.idiomatic: Generally the rich with many sons mostly became officials or monks, exempted from corvée by status;

sentences.zh: 貧人無所入則丁存。

translations.literal: the poor, with nowhere to enter, remained listed as liable men.
translations.idiomatic: the poor, with no such avenue, remained listed as liable men.

sentences.zh: 故課免於上，而賦增於下。

translations.literal: Thus exemptions rose above while levies increased below.
translations.idiomatic: Thus exemptions multiplied above while levies increased below.

sentences.zh: 是以天下殘瘁，蕩為浮人，鄉居地著者百不四五，如是者殆三十年。

translations.literal: Hence all under Heaven was worn to ruin; people drifted as vagrants; those settled in villages and rooted to the land were not four or five in a hundred—thus for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the realm was worn to ruin; people drifted as vagrants; those settled in villages and rooted to the land were scarcely four or five in a hundred—thus for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 炎因奏對，懇言其弊，乃請作兩稅法，以一其名，曰：「凡百役之費，一錢之斂，先度其數而賦於人，量出以制入。

translations.literal: Yan, in memorial response, earnestly spoke of these abuses and then requested the creation of the Two-Tax system, unifying the name, saying: "All expenses of the hundred corvées, every cash of collection—first estimate the amount and levy it upon the people; measure expenditure to regulate income.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, in memorial response, earnestly spoke of these abuses and then proposed the Two-Tax system, unifying the name, saying: "All expenses of the hundred corvées, every cash of collection—first estimate the amount and levy it upon the people; measure expenditure to regulate income.

sentences.zh: 戶無主客，以見居為簿；

translations.literal: Households have no distinction of native or guest—take current residence as the register;
translations.idiomatic: Households have no distinction of native or guest—take current residence as the register;

sentences.zh: 人無丁中，以貧富為差。

translations.literal: persons have no distinction of adult or minor—take rich and poor as the gradation.
translations.idiomatic: persons have no distinction of adult or minor—take rich and poor as the gradation.

sentences.zh: 不居處而行商者，在所郡縣稅三十之一，度所與居者均，使無僥利。

translations.literal: Those who do not reside but travel as merchants shall be taxed one-thirtieth in the prefecture and county where they are; estimate and equalize with residents, so there is no opportunistic profit.
translations.idiomatic: Those who do not reside but travel as merchants shall be taxed one-thirtieth in the prefecture and county where they are; estimate and equalize with residents so there is no opportunistic profit.

sentences.zh: 居人之稅，秋夏兩徵之，俗有不便者正之。

translations.literal: Tax on residents shall be collected twice, in autumn and summer; where custom is inconvenient, correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Tax on residents shall be collected twice, in autumn and summer; where local custom is inconvenient, adjust it.

sentences.zh: 其租庸雜徭悉省，而丁額不廢，申報出入如舊式。

translations.literal: Rent, corvée, and miscellaneous corvées shall all be abolished, yet the adult quota shall not be discarded; reporting of entries and exits shall follow the old form.
translations.idiomatic: Rent, corvée, and miscellaneous corvées shall all be abolished, yet the adult quota shall not be discarded; reporting of entries and exits shall follow the old form.

sentences.zh: 其田畝之稅，率以大曆十四年墾田之數為準而均徵之。

translations.literal: The tax on fields and mu shall uniformly be levied according to the number of reclaimed fields in the fourteenth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: The land tax shall uniformly be levied according to the number of reclaimed fields in Dali 14 (779).

sentences.zh: 夏稅無過六月，秋稅無過十一月。

translations.literal: Summer tax shall not pass the sixth month; autumn tax shall not pass the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax shall not pass the sixth month; autumn tax shall not pass the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 逾歲之後，有戶增而稅減輕，及人散而失均者，進退長吏，而以尚書度支總統焉。」

translations.literal: After the year passes, if households increase yet tax decreases and lightens, or people scatter and equalization is lost, promote or demote the chief local officials, and let the Revenue Commission of the Ministry of Revenue oversee all.
translations.idiomatic: After the year passes, if households increase yet tax decreases, or people scatter and equalization is lost, promote or demote the chief local officials, and let the Revenue Commission of the Ministry of Revenue oversee all.

sentences.zh: 德宗善而行之，詔諭中外。

translations.literal: Dezong approved and implemented it, edicting proclamation within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong approved and implemented it, issuing an edict to proclaim it within and without the court.

sentences.zh: 而掌賦者沮其非利，言租庸之令四百餘年，舊制不可輕改。

translations.literal: Yet those in charge of levies obstructed it as unprofitable, saying the rent-and-corvée order had stood more than four hundred years and the old system must not be lightly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those in charge of levies obstructed it as unprofitable, saying the rent-and-corvée order had stood more than four hundred years and the old system must not be lightly changed.

sentences.zh: 上行之不疑，天下便之。

translations.literal: The emperor carried it out without doubt; all under Heaven found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor carried it out without hesitation; the realm found it a relief.

sentences.zh: 人不土斷而地著，賦不加斂而增入，版籍不造而得其虛實，貪吏不誡而奸無所取。

translations.literal: People were not forcibly bound to the soil yet settled on the land; levies were not increased yet revenue rose; registers were not newly compiled yet reality and emptiness were obtained; greedy officials were not warned yet villainy had nothing to seize.
translations.idiomatic: People were not forcibly bound to the soil yet settled on the land; levies were not increased yet revenue rose; registers were not newly compiled yet the true state of affairs was known; greedy officials were not warned yet villainy had nothing to seize.

sentences.zh: 自是輕重之權，始歸於朝廷。

translations.literal: From this the weight of power began to return to the court.
translations.idiomatic: From this the weight of fiscal power began to return to the court.

sentences.zh: 炎救時之弊，頗有嘉聲。

translations.literal: Yan remedied the abuses of the age and gained considerable praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yan remedied the abuses of the age and won considerable praise.

sentences.zh: 蒞事數月，屬崔祐甫疾病，多不視事，喬琳罷免，炎遂獨當國政。

translations.literal: After several months in office, as Cui Youfu fell ill and largely did not attend to affairs, and Qiao Lin was dismissed and removed, Yan then alone bore state governance.
translations.idiomatic: After several months in office, as Cui Youfu fell ill and largely ceased to attend to affairs and Qiao Lin was dismissed, Yan alone bore state governance.

sentences.zh: 祐甫之所制作，炎隳之。

translations.literal: What Youfu had established, Yan destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: What Youfu had established, Yan tore down.

sentences.zh: 初減薄護作元陵功優，人心始不悅。

translations.literal: At first he reduced and cut the merit rewards for tending construction of Yuan Mausoleum; hearts first turned displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At first he reduced the merit rewards for tending construction of Yuan Mausoleum; public sentiment first turned against him.

sentences.zh: 又專意報恩復仇。

translations.literal: He also devoted himself solely to repaying kindness and taking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: He also devoted himself solely to repaying favors and settling scores.

sentences.zh: 道州錄事參軍王沼有微恩於炎，舉沼為監察御史。

translations.literal: Wang Zhao, recording secretary of Daozhou, had shown Yan a small kindness; Yan recommended Zhao as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhao, recording secretary of Daozhou, had shown Yan a small kindness; Yan recommended Zhao as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 感元載恩，專務行載舊事以報之。

translations.literal: Grateful for Yuan Zai's kindness, he devoted himself to carrying out Zai's old policies to repay him.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Yuan Zai's kindness, he devoted himself to carrying out Zai's old policies to repay him.

sentences.zh: 初，載得罪，左僕射劉晏訊劾之，元載誅，炎亦坐貶，故深怨晏。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Zai fell from grace, Left Vice Director Liu Yan investigated and impeached him; when Yuan Zai was executed, Yan too was implicated and demoted—hence he deeply resented Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Zai fell from grace, Left Vice Director Liu Yan investigated and impeached him; when Yuan Zai was executed, Yang Yan too was implicated and demoted—hence he deeply resented Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 晏領東都、河南、江淮、山南東道轉運、租庸、青苗、鹽鐵使，炎作相數月，欲貶晏，先罷其使，天下錢穀皆歸金部、倉部。

translations.literal: Liu Yan held the commissions of transport, rent-and-corvée, green-sprout, and salt and iron for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jiang-Huai, and Eastern Shannan circuits; several months into his chief ministership, Yang Yan, wishing to demote Liu Yan, first abolished his commissions—all money and grain under Heaven returned to the Gold and Granary bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan held the commissions of transport, rent-and-corvée, green-sprout, and salt and iron for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jiang-Huai, and Eastern Shannan circuits; several months into his chief ministership, Yang Yan, wishing to demote Liu Yan, first abolished his commissions—all money and grain under Heaven returned to the Gold and Granary bureaus.

sentences.zh: 又獻議開豐州陵陽渠，發京畿人夫於西城就役，閭裏騷擾，事竟無成。

translations.literal: He also submitted a proposal to open the Lingyang Canal at Fengzhou, dispatching laborers from the capital region to serve at the western city; villages and lanes were disturbed, and in the end the affair came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a proposal to open the Lingyang Canal at Fengzhou, dispatching laborers from the capital region to serve at the western city; villages and lanes were thrown into turmoil, and in the end the affair came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 初，大曆末，元載議請城原州，以遏西番入寇之沖要，事未行而載誅。

translations.literal: At first, in the late Dali era, Yuan Zai proposed building fortifications at Yuan Prefecture to block the strategic chokepoint of Western Tribes' incursions; the matter had not been carried out when Zai was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the late Dali era, Yuan Zai had proposed fortifying Yuan Prefecture to block the main route of Tibetan incursions, but the plan had not been implemented when Zai was executed.

sentences.zh: 及炎得政，建中二年二月，奏請城原州，先牒涇原節度使段秀實，令為之具。

translations.literal: When Yan came into power, in the second month of the second year of Jianzhong, he memorialized requesting to fortify Yuan Prefecture, first dispatching a note to Jingyuan Military Commissioner Duan Xiushi, ordering him to prepare for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan came to power, in the second month of the second year of Jianzhong (781), he memorialized to fortify Yuan Prefecture and first sent instructions to Jingyuan Military Commissioner Duan Xiushi to make the preparations.

sentences.zh: 秀實報曰：「凡安邊卻敵之長策，宜緩以計圖之，無宜草草興功也。

translations.literal: Xiushi replied: "As for long-term strategies to secure the border and repel enemies, one ought to plan them slowly and deliberately—it is not fitting to launch the work hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi replied: "The best way to secure the frontier and repel enemies is to proceed deliberately with careful planning. It is not wise to rush such a project.

sentences.zh: 又春事方作，請待農隙而緝其事。」

translations.literal: Moreover, spring farming is just beginning; I request that we wait for an agricultural lull before organizing the undertaking."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, spring planting is underway; I ask that we wait until the farming season ends before taking up the matter.

sentences.zh: 炎怒，徵秀實為司農卿。

translations.literal: Yan grew angry and summoned Xiushi to be Minister of the Directorate of Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan was furious and recalled Xiushi to serve as Minister of the Directorate of Grain.

sentences.zh: 以邠寧別駕李懷光居前督作，以檢校司空平章事朱泚、御史大夫平章事崔寧各統兵萬人以翼後。

translations.literal: He put Binning vice-prefect Li Huai'guang in front to supervise the construction, while Acting Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister Zhu Ci and Censor-in-Chief and Associate Chief Minister Cui Ning each commanded ten thousand troops to support the rear.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Binning vice-prefect Li Huai'guang in charge of supervising construction up front, while Acting Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister Zhu Ci and Censor-in-Chief and Associate Chief Minister Cui Ning each led ten thousand troops as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔下涇州為具。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict was issued ordering Jing Prefecture to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, an edict ordered Jing Prefecture to begin preparations.

sentences.zh: 涇軍怒而言曰：「吾曹為國西門之屏，十餘年矣！

translations.literal: The Jing army grew angry and said: "We have been the shield of the nation's western gate for more than ten years!
translations.idiomatic: The troops at Jing were furious and protested: "We have served as the shield of the empire's western gate for more than ten years!

sentences.zh: 始治於邠，才置農桑，地著之安；

translations.literal: We were first settled at Bin, had just established farming and sericulture, and enjoyed the security of living on our land;
translations.idiomatic: We were first established at Bin, had just begun farming and settled into our homes—

sentences.zh: 而徙於此，置榛莽之中，手披足踐，才立城壘；

translations.literal: yet we were moved here, placed amid thorny wilds, clearing paths with our hands and treading with our feet, only then erecting ramparts;
translations.idiomatic: then we were uprooted and sent here to wilderness, hacking through brush with our bare hands and feet before we could even raise the walls;

sentences.zh: 又投之塞外，吾何罪而置此乎！」

translations.literal: and now we are cast beyond the frontier—what crime have we committed to be put in such a place!"
translations.idiomatic: and now we are thrown out to the frontier. What crime have we committed to deserve this!

sentences.zh: 李懷光監朔方軍，法令嚴峻，頻殺大將。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang supervised the Shuofang army; his laws were harsh and stern, and he frequently executed senior generals.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang oversaw the Shuofang army with harsh discipline and repeatedly executed senior commanders.

sentences.zh: 涇州裨將劉文喜因人怨怒，拒不受詔，上疏復求段秀實為帥，否則朱泚。

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture deputy general Liu Wenxi, taking advantage of popular resentment and anger, refused to accept the edict, memorialized requesting that Duan Xiushi be restored as commander, or otherwise Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenxi, a deputy general at Jing Prefecture, stirred by the troops' fury, defied the imperial edict and petitioned to have Duan Xiushi restored as commander—or Zhu Ci if not him.

sentences.zh: 於是以朱泚代懷光，文喜又不奉詔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu Ci was appointed to replace Huai'guang, but Wenxi again refused to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was then sent to replace Huai'guang, but Wenxi again refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 涇有勁兵二萬，閉城拒守，令其子入質吐蕃以求援。

translations.literal: Jing had twenty thousand crack troops; they closed the city and held fast, sending Wenxi's son as a hostage to the Tibetans to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had twenty thousand seasoned troops. They sealed the city gates and held out, sending Wenxi's son to the Tibetans as a hostage to seek reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 時方炎旱，人情騷動，群臣皆請赦文喜，上皆不省。

translations.literal: At the time there was severe drought and public sentiment was agitated; all ministers requested an amnesty for Wenxi, but the emperor paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: A drought was raging and unrest was spreading; ministers urged clemency for Wenxi, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 德宗減服御以給軍人，城中軍士當受春服，賜與如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong reduced his own wardrobe and supplies to provide for the soldiers; the troops in the city who were due spring uniforms received them as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong cut back his own provisions to support the troops, and the garrison inside the city received their spring uniforms as usual.

sentences.zh: 命朱泚、李懷光等軍攻之，乃築壘環之。

translations.literal: He ordered the armies of Zhu Ci, Li Huai'guang, and others to attack, and they built encampments encircling the city.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhu Ci, Li Huai'guang, and other forces to besiege the city, building encampments all around it.

sentences.zh: 涇州別將劉海賓斬文喜首，傳之闕下。

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture lieutenant Liu Haibin beheaded Wenxi and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Haibin, a lieutenant at Jing Prefecture, killed Wenxi and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 茍非海賓效順，必生邊患，皆因炎以喜怒易帥，涇帥結怨故也。

translations.literal: Had Haibin not submitted loyally, a frontier disaster would surely have arisen—all because Yan replaced commanders according to his whims and anger, provoking resentment among the Jing commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Had Haibin not switched sides, a border crisis would surely have erupted—all because Yang Yan capriciously replaced commanders and bred resentment at Jing.

sentences.zh: 原州竟不能城。

translations.literal: In the end Yuan Prefecture was never fortified.
translations.idiomatic: The fortification of Yuan Prefecture was never completed.

sentences.zh: 炎既構劉晏之罪貶官，司農卿庾淮與晏有隙，乃用準為荊南節度使，諷令誣晏以忠州叛，殺之，妻子徙嶺表，朝野為之側目。

translations.literal: After Yan had fabricated Liu Yan's crimes and had him demoted, Minister of the Directorate of Grain Yu Zhun, who had a feud with Liu Yan, was appointed Jingnan military commissioner; Yan instigated him to falsely accuse Liu Yan of rebelling at Zhong Prefecture and had him killed; his wife and children were exiled south of the Ling mountains, and court and countryside looked on aghast.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Yan had framed Liu Yan and had him demoted, Minister of the Directorate of Grain Yu Zhun—who bore a grudge against Liu Yan—was appointed Jingnan military commissioner. Yang Yan prompted him to falsely accuse Liu Yan of rebellion at Zhong Prefecture and had him executed. Liu Yan's wife and children were exiled beyond the Ling mountains, and all of court and countryside looked on in horror.

sentences.zh: 李正己上表請殺晏之罪，指斥朝廷。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji submitted a memorial demanding punishment for killing Liu Yan and rebuked the court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji submitted a memorial calling for accountability for Liu Yan's murder and openly condemned the court.

sentences.zh: 炎懼，乃遣腹心分往諸道：裴冀，東都、河陽、魏博；

translations.literal: Yan, in fear, then dispatched trusted agents to the various circuits: Pei Ji to the Eastern Capital, Heyang, and Weibo;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the backlash, Yang Yan dispatched trusted agents to the various circuits: Pei Ji to the Eastern Capital, Heyang, and Weibo;

sentences.zh: 孫成，澤潞、磁邢、幽州；

translations.literal: Sun Cheng to Zelu, Cixing, and You Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng to Zelu, Cixing, and Youzhou;

sentences.zh: 盧東美，河南、淄青；

translations.literal: Lu Dongmei to Henan and Ziqing;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dongmei to Henan and Ziqing;

sentences.zh: 李舟，山南、湖南；

translations.literal: Li Zhou to Shannan and Hunan;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhou to Shannan and Hunan;

sentences.zh: 王定，淮西。

translations.literal: Wang Ding to Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ding to Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 聲言宣慰，而意實說謗。

translations.literal: They claimed to be on consolation missions, but in intent they were actually spreading slander.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed to be on goodwill missions, but in truth they were spreading slander.

sentences.zh: 且言「晏之得罪，以昔年附會奸邪，謀立獨孤妃為皇后，上自惡之，非他過也。」

translations.literal: And they said: "Liu Yan's crime was that in years past he joined with wicked men in plotting to establish the Consort Dugu as empress—the emperor himself detested this; there was no other offense."
translations.idiomatic: They claimed that "Liu Yan's offense was that years ago he had conspired with corrupt officials to make Consort Dugu empress—a matter the emperor himself loathed. There was no other crime.

sentences.zh: 或有密奏「炎遣五使往諸鎮者，恐天下以殺劉晏之罪歸己，推過於上耳。」

translations.literal: Someone submitted a secret memorial: "Yan sent five envoys to the various circuits because he fears the realm will blame him for Liu Yan's death and is shifting the fault onto the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Someone submitted a secret memorial: "Yang Yan sent five envoys to the military circuits because he fears the empire will hold him responsible for Liu Yan's death and is trying to shift the blame onto the emperor.

sentences.zh: 乃使中人復炎辭於正己，還報信然。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent a palace attendant to repeat Yan's words to Zhengji, and the report confirmed they were true.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace attendant to relay Yang Yan's words back to Li Zhengji, and the report confirmed that they were indeed what Yan had said.

sentences.zh: 自此德宗有意誅炎矣，待事而發。

translations.literal: From this Emperor Dezong intended to execute Yan and waited for an occasion to act.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Emperor Dezong resolved to destroy Yang Yan and waited for the right opportunity.

sentences.zh: 乃擢用盧杞為門下侍郎、平章事，炎轉中書侍郎，仍平章事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lu Qi was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Chief Minister; Yan was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, still Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Chief Minister; Yang Yan was moved to Vice Director of the Secretariat but remained Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 二人同事秉政，杞無文學，儀貌寢陋，炎惡而忽之，每托疾息於他閣，多不會食，杞亦銜恨之。

translations.literal: The two served together in holding power; Qi had no literary attainments and his appearance was unsightly; Yan despised and slighted him, often pleading illness to rest in another pavilion and frequently not dining together—Qi also nursed resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: The two served together as chief ministers. Qi had no scholarly distinction and cut a homely figure. Yang Yan despised and slighted him, often feigning illness to withdraw to another hall and rarely dining with him—Qi nursed a deep grudge in return.

sentences.zh: 舊制，中書舍人分押尚書六曹，以平奏報，開元初廢其職，杞請復之，炎固以為不可。

translations.literal: Under the old system, secretariat drafters were assigned to oversee the six bureaus of the Ministry of State to equalize memorials and reports; in the early Kaiyuan era this duty was abolished; Qi requested its restoration, but Yan firmly held it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Under an old arrangement, secretariat drafters had overseen the six bureaus of the Ministry of State to review memorials and reports; this had been abolished in early Kaiyuan. Lu Qi requested its restoration, but Yang Yan firmly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 杞益怒，又密啟中書主書過，逐之。

translations.literal: Qi grew still angrier and secretly reported offenses by the chief clerks of the Secretariat, having them expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi grew angrier still and secretly reported misconduct by the chief clerks of the Secretariat, having them expelled.

sentences.zh: 炎怒曰：「主書，吾局吏也，有過吾自治之，奈何而相侵？」

translations.literal: Yan grew angry and said: "The chief clerks are my bureau's subordinates; if they have faults I will discipline them myself—how dare you encroach on my authority?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan erupted in anger: "The chief clerks are my own staff. If they err, I will discipline them myself—how dare you interfere?"

sentences.zh: 屬梁崇義叛換，德宗欲以淮西節度使李希烈統諸軍討之。

translations.literal: Just then Liang Chongyi rebelled and turned traitor; Emperor Dezong wished to put Huaixi Military Commissioner Li Sixi in overall command of the armies to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liang Chongyi rebelled; Emperor Dezong wanted to put Huaixi Military Commissioner Li Sixi in overall command of the forces to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 炎諫曰：「希烈始與李忠臣為子，親任無雙，竟逐忠臣而取其位，背本若此，豈可信也！

translations.literal: Yan remonstrated: "Sixi at first became Li Zhongchen's adopted son and was trusted above all others, yet in the end he drove Zhongchen out and seized his position—having betrayed his origins like this, how can he be trusted!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan objected: "Li Sixi was once Li Zhongchen's adopted son and enjoyed his complete trust, yet he eventually drove Zhongchen out and took his place. A man who betrays his benefactor like this—how can he be trusted!

sentences.zh: 居常無尺寸功，猶強不奉法，異日平賊後，恃功邀上，陛下何以馭之？」

translations.literal: In ordinary times he has not the slightest merit, yet he is already strong and refuses to obey the law—if someday, after the rebels are pacified, he relies on his achievements to make demands of Your Majesty, how will you control him?"
translations.idiomatic: He has accomplished nothing of note, yet already defies the law. If one day, after the rebels are crushed, he uses his military success to make demands on Your Majesty, how will you restrain him?

sentences.zh: 初，炎之南來，途經襄、漢，固勸崇義入朝，崇義不能從，已懷反側。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yan came south, he passed through Xiang and Han and had firmly urged Chongyi to enter court; Chongyi could not comply and already harbored disloyal thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yang Yan traveled south, he had passed through Xiang and Han and strongly urged Chongyi to come to court. Chongyi refused, and resentment had already taken root.

sentences.zh: 尋又使其黨李舟使馳說，崇義固而拒命，遂圖叛逆，皆炎迫而成之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also sent his follower Li Zhou on a fast mission to persuade him; Chongyi hardened in refusing orders and then plotted rebellion—all forced into being by Yan's pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan then sent his ally Li Zhou on an urgent mission to persuade him, but Chongyi only dug in his heels and refused orders, eventually plotting rebellion—all outcomes Yang Yan's pressure had brought about.

sentences.zh: 至是，德宗欲假希烈兵勢以討崇義，然後別圖希烈。

translations.literal: At this point Emperor Dezong wished to borrow Sixi's military strength to attack Chongyi, and afterward make separate plans against Sixi.
translations.idiomatic: By now Emperor Dezong intended to borrow Li Sixi's military strength to crush Chongyi, then deal with Sixi separately.

sentences.zh: 炎又固言不可，上不能平，乃曰：「朕業許之矣，不能食言。」

translations.literal: Yan again firmly said it could not be done; the emperor could not be reconciled and said: "I have already promised it and cannot go back on my word."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan again insisted it was unwise. The emperor, unable to accept his counsel, said: "I have already given my word and cannot take it back.

sentences.zh: 遂以希烈統諸軍。

translations.literal: Sixi was thereupon put in overall command of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sixi was then placed in overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 會德宗嘗訪宰相群臣中可以大任者，盧杞薦張鎰、嚴郢，而炎舉崔昭、趙惠伯。

translations.literal: Once Emperor Dezong consulted the chief ministers and the assembled ministers on who could be entrusted with great responsibility, Lu Qi recommended Zhang Yi and Yan Ying, while Yan recommended Cui Zhao and Zhao Huibo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong asked the chief ministers and the assembled officials who could be entrusted with great responsibility, Lu Qi recommended Zhang Yi and Yan Ying, while Yang Yan recommended Cui Zhao and Zhao Huibo.

sentences.zh: 上以炎論議疏闊，遂罷炎相，為左僕射。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Yan's policy discussions shallow and broad, and thereupon dismissed him as chief minister, appointing him Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found Yang Yan's policy counsel shallow and impractical and removed him as chief minister, appointing him Left Vice Director instead.

sentences.zh: 後數日中謝，對於延英，及出，馳歸，不至中書，盧杞自是益怒焉。

translations.literal: Several days later, when he came to offer thanks, he was received in the Yanying Hall; upon leaving he galloped home and did not go to the Secretariat—Lu Qi from this grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, when Yang Yan came to offer thanks and was received in the Yanying Hall, he rode straight home afterward without stopping at the Secretariat—Lu Qi was enraged all the more.

sentences.zh: 杞尋引嚴郢為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Qi soon brought in Yan Ying as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi soon appointed Yan Ying Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 初，郢為京兆尹，不附炎，炎怒之，諷御史張著彈郢，郢罷兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Ying was metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he did not attach himself to Yan; Yan grew angry and instigated censor Zhang Zhu to impeach Ying, and Ying was removed from his concurrent post as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yan Ying had served as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he had refused to align with Yang Yan. Yang Yan, angered, prompted censor Zhang Zhu to impeach him, and Yan Ying lost his concurrent post as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 炎又夙聞源休與郢有隙，乃拔休自流人為京兆尹，令伺郢過。

translations.literal: Yan had also long heard that Yuan Xiu and Ying had a feud, and so promoted Xiu from exile to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, ordering him to watch for Ying's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had also long known of the feud between Yuan Xiu and Yan Ying, and so promoted Xiu from exile to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, instructing him to watch for Ying's missteps.

sentences.zh: 休蒞官後，與郢友善，炎大怒。

translations.literal: After Xiu took office he became friendly with Ying, and Yan flew into a rage.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, however, Xiu became friendly with Yan Ying, and Yang Yan was furious.

sentences.zh: 張光晟方謀議殺回紇酋帥，炎乃以休為入回紇使，休幾為虜所殺。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangcheng was then plotting to kill the Uyghur chieftain; Yan therefore appointed Xiu envoy to the Uyghurs, and Xiu nearly lost his life to capture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangcheng was then plotting to kill the Uyghur chieftain; Yang Yan therefore sent Xiu as envoy to the Uyghurs, and Xiu nearly died at their hands.

sentences.zh: 郢尋坐以度田不實，改為大理卿，時人惜之。

translations.literal: Ying soon fell from office on the charge that his land-survey figures were false and was transferred to minister of justice; people of the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying was soon removed on charges of falsifying land-survey records and transferred to minister of justice; many regretted his fall.

sentences.zh: 至是，杞因群情所欲，又知郢與炎有隙，故引薦之。

translations.literal: At this point Qi, following what public sentiment desired and knowing that Ying and Yan had a feud, therefore recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lu Qi, acting on public sentiment and knowing of the rift between Yan Ying and Yang Yan, deliberately recommended him.

sentences.zh: 炎子弘業不肖，多犯禁，受賂請托，郢按之，兼得其他過。

translations.literal: Yan's son Hongye was unworthy, repeatedly violating prohibitions and accepting bribes and entreaties; Ying investigated him and also uncovered other offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan's son Hongye was a dissolute man who repeatedly broke the law and accepted bribes and favors; Yan Ying investigated him and uncovered further offenses as well.

sentences.zh: 初，炎將立家廟，先有私第在東都，令河南尹趙惠伯貨之，惠伯為炎市為官廨。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Yan was about to establish his family temple, he already had a private residence in the Eastern Capital and ordered Henan Magistrate Zhao Huibo to sell it; Huibo purchased it for Yan as an official office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yang Yan planned to build his family temple, he already owned a private residence in the Eastern Capital and had Henan Magistrate Zhao Huibo sell it; Huibo bought the property on Yang Yan's behalf as an official office.

sentences.zh: 時惠伯自河中尹、都團練觀察等使初受代，郢奏追捕惠伯詰案。

translations.literal: At the time Huibo had just been relieved of his posts as metropolitan magistrate of Hezhong and military governor and observation commissioner; Ying memorialized to pursue and interrogate Huibo in the case.
translations.idiomatic: Huibo had just been relieved of his posts as metropolitan magistrate of Hezhong and military governor and observation commissioner; Yan Ying memorialized to have him pursued and interrogated.

sentences.zh: 御史以炎為宰相，抑吏貨市私第，貴估其宅，賤入其幣，計以為贓。

translations.literal: The censors held that as chief minister Yan had suppressed officials in selling his private residence, overvaluing the house and undervaluing the payment—calculated as embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: The censors charged that as chief minister, Yang Yan had coerced officials into buying his private residence at an inflated price while accepting an undervalued payment—amounting to embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 杞召大理正田晉評罪，晉曰：「宰臣於庶官，比之監臨，官市賈有羨利，計其利以乞取論罪，當奪官。」

translations.literal: Qi summoned Grand Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Tian Jin to assess the crime; Jin said: "When a chief minister deals with a subordinate official, it is comparable to supervision; if in an official purchase there is surplus profit, calculating that profit as solicited gain for sentencing, the penalty should be removal from office."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi summoned Grand Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Tian Jin to assess the crime. Jin ruled: "When a chief minister deals with a subordinate, it is comparable to supervision. If an official purchase yields surplus profit, and that profit is counted as solicited gain, the penalty should be removal from office.

sentences.zh: 杞怒，謫晉衡州司馬。

translations.literal: Qi grew angry and demoted Jin to assistant magistrate of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi was furious and demoted Jin to assistant magistrate of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 更召他吏繩之，曰：「監主自盜，罪絞。」

translations.literal: He then summoned another official to apply the law and said: "A supervisor who steals on his own authority—punishment by strangulation."
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned another official to apply the law and ruled: "A supervisor who steals on his own authority is punishable by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 開元中，蕭嵩將於曲江南立私廟，尋以玄宗臨幸之所，恐置廟非便，乃罷之。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Xiao Song was about to establish a private temple south of Qujiang; soon afterward, because it was a place Emperor Xuanzong visited, he feared placing a temple there would be inappropriate and abandoned the plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era, Xiao Song had planned to build a private temple south of Qujiang, but abandoned the idea when he realized it was a place Emperor Xuanzong frequented.

sentences.zh: 至是，炎以其地為廟，有飛語者云：「此地有王氣，炎故取之，必有異圖。」

translations.literal: At this point Yan made that site his temple; someone spread rumors saying: "This place has royal qi; Yan therefore took it because he harbors treasonous designs."
translations.idiomatic: Now Yang Yan built his temple on that very site. Rumors spread that "this place possesses the aura of kingship; Yang Yan seized it because he harbors treasonous ambitions.

sentences.zh: 語聞，上愈怒。

translations.literal: When the words reached the emperor, he grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor, his anger only deepened.

sentences.zh: 及臺司上具獄，詔三司使同覆之。

translations.literal: When the censorate submitted the complete case, an edict ordered the Three Offices to review it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When the censorate submitted the full case, an edict ordered the Three Offices to review it jointly.

sentences.zh: 建中二年十月，詔曰：「尚書左僕射楊炎，托以文藝，累登清貫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Jianzhong, an edict said: "Left Vice Director Yang Yan, relying on literary talent, repeatedly rose to honorable posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Jianzhong, an edict declared: "Left Vice Director Yang Yan, trading on literary talent, rose repeatedly to honorable posts.

sentences.zh: 雖謫居荒服，而虛稱猶存。

translations.literal: Though demoted to live in a remote region, his empty reputation still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Though once demoted to a remote frontier, his reputation still lingered.

sentences.zh: 朕初臨萬邦，思弘大化，務擢非次，招納時髦。

translations.literal: When I first assumed rule over the myriad states, I thought to expand great transformation, striving to promote men out of turn and recruit the outstanding of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When I first ascended the throne, I sought to enact great reforms, promoting men out of turn and recruiting the finest talent of the age.

sentences.zh: 拔自郡佐，登於鼎司，獨委心膂，信任無疑。

translations.literal: Raised from a prefectural aide to the highest ministry, I entrusted him alone as my right hand, trusting him without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: I raised him from a prefectural aide to the highest ministry, entrusting him as my right hand without a moment's doubt.

sentences.zh: 而乃不思竭誠，敢為奸蠹，進邪醜正，既偽且堅，黨援因依，動涉情故。

translations.literal: Yet he did not think to exhaust his loyalty but dared to act as a wicked parasite, advancing the wicked and displacing the upright—both false and stubborn, forming factions and relying on connections, his actions always tangled in personal ties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet instead of serving with full loyalty, he acted as a corrupt parasite—promoting the wicked, displacing the upright, obstinate in deceit, building factions and trading on personal connections at every turn.

sentences.zh: 隳法敗度，罔上行私，茍利其身，不顧於國。

translations.literal: He destroyed the law and ruined standards, deceived his superiors and pursued private ends, seeking profit for himself without regard for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He undermined law and propriety, deceived his sovereign, and pursued private gain without regard for the state.

sentences.zh: 加以內無訓誡，外有交通，縱恣詐欺，以成贓賄。

translations.literal: Moreover, within he lacked instruction and restraint, without he maintained illicit contacts, indulging in fraud and deceit until bribery and corruption were complete.
translations.idiomatic: At home he lacked moral restraint; abroad he maintained illicit contacts, indulging in fraud until bribery and corruption were complete.

sentences.zh: 詢其事跡，本末乖謬，蔑恩棄德，負我何深！

translations.literal: Inquiring into the facts of his conduct, beginning and end were perverse; he scorned kindness and abandoned virtue—how deeply he has betrayed me!
translations.idiomatic: Examining the facts of his conduct, the whole record is a tangle of perversity. He scorned kindness and abandoned virtue—how deeply he has betrayed my trust!

sentences.zh: 考狀議刑，罪在難宥。

translations.literal: Reviewing the evidence and deliberating punishment, his guilt admits no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the evidence and weighing the penalty, his guilt admits no pardon.

sentences.zh: 但以朕於將相，義切始終，顧全大體，特有弘貸，俾從遠謫，以肅具僚。

translations.literal: Yet because in my dealings with generals and ministers I am bound by the principle of seeing things through, considering the larger interest I specially grant leniency, allowing exile to a distant post to admonish all officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because I hold generals and ministers to the bond of loyalty from first to last, and for the sake of the larger interest I grant special leniency, exiling him to a distant post as a warning to all officials.

sentences.zh: 可崖州司馬同正，仍馳驛發遣。」

translations.literal: He is appointed Assistant Magistrate of Yazhou with concurrent regular rank, and is to be dispatched immediately by post relay."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Assistant Magistrate of Yazhou with concurrent regular rank, to be dispatched immediately by post relay.

sentences.zh: 去崖州百里賜死，年五十五。

translations.literal: One hundred li from Yazhou he was granted death; he was fifty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred li from Yazhou he was granted death by imperial order. He was fifty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 炎早有文章，亦勵誌節，及為中書舍人，附會元載，時議已薄之。

translations.literal: Yan early possessed literary talent and also cultivated integrity; when he became secretariat drafter he attached himself to Yuan Zai, and public opinion already held him in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had literary talent from early on and cultivated a reputation for integrity, but when he became secretariat drafter he attached himself to Yuan Zai, and public opinion already looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 後坐載貶官，憤恚益甚，歸而得政，睚眥必仇，險害之性附於心，唯其愛憎，不顧公道，以至於敗。

translations.literal: Later, implicated in Zai's fall and demoted, his resentment grew still greater; once back in power he repaid every grudge, and his treacherous and harmful nature attached itself to his heart—following only his loves and hates without regard for public justice, until ruin.
translations.idiomatic: After he was implicated in Zai's fall and demoted, his resentment only deepened. Once back in power he repaid every slight; his treacherous nature took hold of his heart, and he followed only personal likes and dislikes without regard for justice—until his downfall.

sentences.zh: 惠伯亦坐炎貶費州多田尉，尋亦殺之。

translations.literal: Huibo was also implicated because of Yan and demoted to registrar of Duotian in Fei Prefecture; soon afterward he too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huibo was also implicated through Yang Yan and demoted to registrar of Duotian in Fei Prefecture; he too was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 黎幹黎幹者，戎州人。

translations.literal: Li Gan. Li Gan was a man of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan. Li Gan was a native of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始以善星緯數術進，待詔翰林，累官至諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At first he advanced through skill in astronomy, calendrics, and numerology, served as Hanlin attendant, and rose through repeated promotions to Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He first rose through skill in astronomy, calendrics, and numerology, served as Hanlin attendant, and rose through repeated promotions to Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 尋遷京兆尹，以嚴肅為理，人頗便之，而因緣附會，與時上下。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao; he governed with severity and the people found it convenient, yet he also attached himself to the powerful and rose and fell with the times.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, where his stern governance won public approval, yet he also curried favor with the powerful and rose and fell with the political winds.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年，改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali, he was transferred to vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dali (767), he was transferred to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩伏誅，坐交通出為桂州刺史、本管觀察使。

translations.literal: When Yu Chaoen was executed, Gan was implicated for illicit contact and sent out as prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chaoen was executed, Gan was implicated for illicit contact and sent out as prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of his circuit.

sentences.zh: 至江陵，丁母憂。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiangling, he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jiangling, he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，會京兆尹缺，人頗思幹。

translations.literal: After a long time, when the post of metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao fell vacant, people greatly missed Gan.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, when the post of metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao fell vacant, many missed Gan's tenure.

sentences.zh: 八年，復拜京兆尹、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was again appointed metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (773), he was again appointed metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 幹自以得誌，無心為理，貪暴益甚，徇於財色。

translations.literal: Gan, considering that he had achieved his ambition, had no heart for governance; his greed and cruelty grew still worse, and he indulged in wealth and women.
translations.idiomatic: Gan, feeling he had achieved his ambition, lost interest in governing; his greed and cruelty grew worse, and he indulged in wealth and women.

sentences.zh: 十三年，除兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was appointed vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (778), he was appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 性險，挾左道，結中貴，以希主恩，代宗甚惑之。

translations.literal: By nature he was treacherous; he practiced heterodox arts, cultivated ties with palace eunuchs, and sought imperial favor—Emperor Daizong was greatly deluded by him.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous by nature, he practiced heterodox arts, cultivated ties with palace eunuchs, and sought imperial favor—Emperor Daizong was greatly taken in by him.

sentences.zh: 時中官劉忠翼寵任方盛，幹結之素厚，嘗通其奸謀。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Liu Zhongyi's favor and trust were at their height; Gan had long been closely tied to him and had once communicated his treasonous plots.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the eunuch Liu Zhongyi enjoyed peak favor and trust; Gan had long been closely tied to him and had once communicated his treasonous plots.

sentences.zh: 及德宗初即位，幹猶以詭道求進，密居輿中詣忠翼第。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong first ascended the throne, Gan still sought advancement through deceitful means, secretly riding in a litter to visit Zhongyi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong first ascended the throne, Gan still sought advancement through deceitful means, secretly riding in a closed litter to visit Zhongyi's residence.

sentences.zh: 事發，詔曰：「兵部侍郎黎幹，害若豺狼，特進劉忠翼，掩義隱賊，並除名長流。」

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, an edict said: "Vice Minister of War Li Gan, vicious as a wolf; Special Advance Liu Zhongyi, concealing righteousness and harboring a villain—both are stripped of rank and exiled to distant posts."
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, an edict declared: "Vice Minister of War Li Gan, vicious as a wolf; Special Advance Liu Zhongyi, concealing righteousness and harboring a villain—both are stripped of rank and exiled to distant posts.

sentences.zh: 即行，市里兒童數千人噪聚，懷瓦礫投擊之，捕賊尉不能止，遂皆賜死於藍田驛。

translations.literal: As they set out, several thousand children in the marketplaces gathered noisily, holding tiles and stones to pelt them; the thief-catching constable could not stop them, and both were granted death at Lantian Post.
translations.idiomatic: As they set out, several thousand townspeople and children gathered, pelting them with tiles and stones; the constable could not restrain the mob, and both were granted death at Lantian Post.

sentences.zh: 附 劉忠翼忠翼，宦官也，本名清潭，與董秀皆有寵於代宗。

translations.literal: Appendix: Liu Zhongyi. Zhongyi was a eunuch; his original name was Qingtan; he and Dong Xiu both enjoyed favor with Emperor Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Liu Zhongyi. Zhongyi was a eunuch; his original name was Qingtan; he and Dong Xiu both enjoyed favor with Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 天憲在口，勢回日月，貪饕納賄，貨產巨萬。

translations.literal: Heaven's law was in his mouth and his power turned sun and moon; he was insatiably greedy, accepting bribes until his assets reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke as though he wielded Heaven's law, and his power eclipsed sun and moon; insatiably greedy, he accepted bribes until his wealth reached tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，德宗居東宮，幹及清潭嘗有奸謀動搖。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, when Dezong resided in the Eastern Palace, Gan and Qingtan once had treacherous plots to shake the succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, when Dezong was crown prince, Gan and Qingtan once plotted treacherously against the succession.

sentences.zh: 及是，積前罪以誅之。

translations.literal: On this occasion, their accumulated earlier crimes were the grounds for executing them.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion they were executed for their accumulated earlier crimes.

sentences.zh: 庾準庾準，常州人。

translations.literal: Yu Zhun. Yu Zhun was a man of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhun. Yu Zhun was a native of Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父光先，天寶中，文部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Guangxian was vice director in the Ministry of Rites in the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangxian was vice director in the Ministry of Rites during the Tianbao reign.

sentences.zh: 準以門入仕，昵於宰相王縉，縉驟引至職方郎中、知制誥，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Zhun entered office through family connections, became intimate with Chief Minister Wang Jin, and Jin swiftly promoted him to director in the Bureau of Appointments with charge of drafting edicts, then to drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun entered office through family connections, became intimate with Chief Minister Wang Jin, who swiftly promoted him to director in the Bureau of Appointments with charge of drafting edicts, then to drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 準素寡文學，以柔媚自進，既非儒流，甚為時論所薄。

translations.literal: Zhun had always lacked literary learning and advanced himself through soft flattery; since he was not of the Confucian stream, he was much despised in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun had always lacked literary learning and advanced himself through flattery; since he was not a true scholar, he was much despised in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 尋改御史中丞，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to vice censor-in-chief and promoted to left vice director in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed vice censor-in-chief and promoted to left vice director in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 縉得罪，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jin fell from grace, Zhun was sent out as prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell from grace, Zhun was sent out as prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 復入為司農卿，與楊炎厚善。

translations.literal: He re-entered the capital as minister of agriculture and was on close terms with Yang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as minister of agriculture and was on close terms with Yang Yan.

sentences.zh: 炎欲殺劉晏，知準與晏有隙，乃用為荊南節度。

translations.literal: Yan wished to kill Liu Yan and, knowing that Zhun bore a grudge against Yan, appointed him military commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan wished to kill Liu Yan and, knowing that Zhun bore a grudge against him, appointed Zhun military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 準乃上言得晏與朱泚書，且有怨望，又召補州兵以拒命。

translations.literal: Zhun then memorialized that he had obtained letters between Yan and Zhu Ci, that Yan harbored resentment, and that he had also summoned and supplemented prefectural troops to resist orders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun then memorialized that he had obtained letters between Liu Yan and Zhu Ci, that Yan harbored resentment, and that he had also summoned prefectural troops to resist orders.

sentences.zh: 於是先殺晏，然後下詔賜自盡，海內冤之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan was killed first; only then was an edict issued granting him death by his own hand. All within the seas considered it a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Liu Yan was killed first; only then was an edict issued ordering him to take his own life. The empire considered it a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 炎以殺晏徵準為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Yan, for killing Yan, summoned Zhun back as left vice director in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For killing Liu Yan, Yang Yan summoned Zhun back as left vice director in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 建中三年六月丁巳卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the sixth month of the third year of Jianzhong he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the sixth month of the third year of Jianzhong (782) he died, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title of minister of works.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：仲尼云：富與貴是人之欲，不以道得之不處。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The historiographer says: Confucius said: Wealth and honor are what people desire; if they are not obtained by the Way, one does not dwell in them.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Confucius said: Wealth and honor are what people desire; if they are not obtained by the Way, one does not dwell in them.

sentences.zh: 反乎是道者小人。

translations.literal: Those who oppose this Way are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Those who oppose this Way are petty men.

sentences.zh: 載諂輔國以進身，弄時權而固位，眾怒難犯，長惡不悛，家亡而誅及妻兒，身死而殃及祖禰。

translations.literal: Zai flattered Fuguo to advance himself, manipulated timely power to secure his position, provoked anger none could withstand, and persisted in evil without repentance; his house was destroyed and punishment reached wife and children, his body died and calamity reached ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Zai flattered Li Fuguo to advance himself, manipulated power to secure his position, provoked universal anger, and persisted in evil without repentance; his house was destroyed and punishment reached wife and children, his body died and calamity reached his ancestors.

sentences.zh: 縉附會奸邪，以至顛覆。

translations.literal: Jin attached himself to the wicked and thereby reached ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin attached himself to the wicked and thereby reached ruin.

sentences.zh: 炎隳崔祐甫之規，怒段秀實之直，酬恩報怨，以私害公。

translations.literal: Yan destroyed Cui Youfu's regulations, resented Duan Xiushi's uprightness, repaid favors and avenged grudges, and harmed the public with private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Yan destroyed Cui Youfu's regulations, resented Duan Xiushi's uprightness, repaid favors and avenged grudges, and harmed the public with private ends.

sentences.zh: 三子者咸著文章，殊乖德行。

translations.literal: All three were accomplished in literary composition yet greatly at odds with moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All three were accomplished in literary composition yet greatly at odds with moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 「不常其德，或承之羞」，大《易》之義也。

translations.literal: "If one does not hold fast to virtue, one may inherit disgrace"—this is the meaning of the Great Changes.
translations.idiomatic: "If one does not hold fast to virtue, one may inherit disgrace"—this is the meaning of the Great Changes.

sentences.zh: 富貴不以其道，小人之事哉！

translations.literal: Wealth and honor not by the Way—are these not the affairs of petty men!
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and honor not obtained by the Way—are these not the affairs of petty men!

sentences.zh: 觀庾準之憸，遭王縉之復，徇楊炎之意，曲致劉晏之冤。

translations.literal: Observe Yu Zhun's sycophancy, his encounter with Wang Jin's favor, his following Yang Yan's intent, and his crooked bringing about of Liu Yan's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yu Zhun's sycophancy, his rise through Wang Jin's favor, his following Yang Yan's intent, and his crooked bringing about of Liu Yan's unjust death.

sentences.zh: 積惡而獲令終者，其在餘殃乎！

translations.literal: One who accumulates evil yet obtains a peaceful end—perhaps the remaining retribution is yet to come!
translations.idiomatic: One who accumulates evil yet dies a peaceful death—perhaps the remaining retribution is yet to come!

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：載、縉、炎、準，交相附會。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Zai, Jin, Yan, and Zhun attached themselves to one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary says: Zai, Jin, Yan, and Zhun attached themselves to one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 《左傳》有言，貪人敗類。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary has a saying: the greedy man ruins his kind.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: the greedy man ruins his kind.
